핵심 시사점: Nasdaq 기술이 글로벌 배포 범위는 가장 넓지만, 대형 거래소(NYSE, CME, Euronext, HKEX 주식, 중국 거래소)는 자체개발 시스템을 사용한다. Tier 1 거래소는 자체개발, Tier 2/3 거래소는 라이선스 기술을 채택하는 추세가 뚜렷하다.




1.3 청산기관 관계도 — CCP별 청산 대상 거래소 (Clearing Relationship Map — Which CCP Clears for Which Exchange)

글로벌 CCP-거래소 관계
DTCC (NSCC/DTC/FICC)
  ├── NYSE
  ├── NASDAQ
  ├── Cboe (주식)
  └── 모든 미국 주식 거래소 + 미국 국채

CME Clearing
  ├── CME / CBOT / NYMEX / COMEX
  ├── DME (Dubai Mercantile Exchange)
  └── FICC (국채)와 교차증거금

OCC (Options Clearing Corporation)
  ├── 모든 미국 주식옵션 거래소 (Cboe, NYSE Arca, NASDAQ, ISE 등)
  └── NSCC/FICC/DTC와 교차증거금

LCH Ltd (영국)
  ├── LSE (EquityClear)
  ├── 글로벌 OTC IRS (SwapClear — 2024년 상반기 $779T)
  ├── RepoClear
  └── 상호운용성: SIX x-clear, Cboe Clear Europe

Euronext Clearing (구 LCH SA, 2024년 9월 전환)
  ├── Euronext (파리, 암스테르담, 브뤼셀, 리스본, 더블린, 오슬로, 밀라노)
  └── Borsa Italiana (전환 중)

Eurex Clearing
  ├── Eurex (파생상품)
  ├── Xetra / Deutsche Borse (주식)
  ├── Nasdaq Nordic
  └── OTC IRS 청산

JSCC (일본)
  ├── TSE / JPX (주식)
  ├── Osaka Exchange (파생상품)
  └── OTC IRS (TONA), CDS

HKEX Clearing (HKSCC / HKCC / SEOCH)
  ├── HKEX (주식, HKSCC 경유)

SGX-DC / CDP

ICE Clear (US / Europe / Credit)
  ├── ICE Futures U.S.
  ├── ICE Futures Europe

ASX Clear / ASX Clear (Futures)

ChinaClear (CSDC)

2. KRX 벤치마킹 (KRX Benchmarking)

2.1 KRX 프로필 요약 (KRX Profile Summary)
Korea Exchange (KRX, 한국거래소)는 주식(KOSPI/KOSDAQ/KONEX), 파생상품, 채권을 아우르는 통합 거래소로 운영된다. 핵심 인프라는 다음과 같다.

주식 매매시스템: Exture 3.0 (1단계: 2023년 1월, 2단계: 2023년 10월; 자체개발)
파생상품 매매시스템: Exture 3.0 (통합 플랫폼)
CCP: KRX가 전체 상장상품에 대해 직접 CCP 역할 수행
CSD: KSD (한국예탁결제원, Korea Securities Depository)
감독기관: FSC (금융위원회, Financial Services Commission), FSS (금융감독원, Financial Supervisory Service), BOK (한국은행, Bank of Korea — 시스템적 감독)
결제주기: T+2 (주식), T+1 (국채), T+0/T+1 (파생상품 증거금)
시가총액: 약 KRW 4,277조 (약 USD 2.95조, 2026년 1월)
상장기업 수: 약 2,901개 (KOSPI 약 954개, KOSDAQ 1,700개 이상, KONEX 약 129개)
일평균 거래대금: 약 KRW 32.23조 (약 USD 207억, 2026년 2월 평균)

평가: - 경쟁력 있음: Exture 3.0 지연시간(약 49μs 최악치 추정)은 대부분의 거래소와 비교 시 경쟁력이 있으나, 선두 거래소(T7 약 5μs, NASDAQ 약 14μs)에는 미치지 못한다. - 강점: Exture 3.0은 최근(2023년 1월/10월) 업그레이드된 시스템으로, 저지연 범위를 청산·결제까지 확장한 통합 플랫폼을 제공 — 대부분의 비교 대상보다 커버리지가 넓다. - 강점: 주식, 파생상품, 청산·결제를 아우르는 통합 플랫폼 — arrowhead + J-GATE + JSCC와 같이 시스템이 분리된 JPX보다 효율적이다. - 격차: 공식적인 Exture 3.0 지연시간·처리량이 공개되지 않음 — 약 49μs 수치는 KRX가 발표한 EXTURE+(≤70μs) 대비 30% 개선 주장에 근거한 추정치이다.

결제이행재원 상세 데이터를 포함한 CPMI-IOSCO PQD 보고서 발간
CCP 회복·정리 계획 문서 강화

중동/아프리카 규제: 중동 또는 아프리카에 대한 전용 규제 파일 없음. 거래소 수준 문서(Tadawul, JSE, DME) 내에서 간략히 다루어짐.
OTC 파생상품 청산: 주요 CCP(LCH SwapClear, CME OTC, Eurex OTC)를 제외한 양자 대 청산 OTC 시장에 대한 상세 내용 제한적.

Exture 3.0 공식 지연시간 및 처리량 사양 (KRX 미공개; 약 49μs는 30% 개선 주장에 근거한 추정치)

section: 4. 2026년 10월 20일 현재 기준 주요 현행화 및 시장 제도 업데이트 (October 2026 Regulatory & Market Infrastructure Updates)
text:
4. 2026년 10월 20일 현재 기준 주요 현행화 및 시장 제도 업데이트 (October 2026 Regulatory & Market Infrastructure Updates)
본 조사의 기준 시점인 2026년 10월 20일 현재, 글로벌 거래소 및 청산·결제 인프라는 ATS와의 복수 경쟁 체제 정착, T+1 결제주기 단축의 글로벌 확산, 24시간 연장 거래 인프라 확충, 그리고 AI·클라우드 기반 시장감시 및 DORA(디지털 운영 복원력) 체계의 전면적 의무화를 맞이하고 있다.

4.1 한국 자본시장: ATS 출범 이후 복수 시장 체제 및 IT 인프라 고도화

대체거래소(ATS) 넥스트레이드(Nextrade) 안착 및 SOR(Smart Order Routing) 가동:

2025년 3월 공식 출범한 한국 최초의 대체거래소 넥스트레이드는 2026년 10월 현재 코스피·코스닥 주요 종목에 대해 거래대금 점유율 10~15% 수준에 안착했다.
거래시간(08:00~20:00, 12시간 운영) 차별화에 대응하여, 증권사들의 최선집행의무(Best Execution) 이행을 위한 자동주문전송(SOR) 엔진이 KRX와 넥스트레이드 간 가격·수수료·수량을 실시간 비교하여 최적 시장으로 주문을 분기하고 있다.
KRX는 이에 대응하여 중간가 호가, 스톱지정가 호가 등 신규 주문 유형의 성공적 정착 및 메이커-테이커(Maker-Taker) 유동성 공급 수수료 체계를 고도화하여 정규 시장 유동성을 수호하고 있다.

공매도 전산시스템(NSDS, 무차입공매도 중앙차단 시스템) 전면 안착:

2025년 3월 31일 공매도 재개와 함께 가동된 한국거래소 NSDS(National Short-sale Detecting System)가 2026년 10월 현재 완벽하게 정착되었다.
기관투자자의 내부 독립 잔고관리시스템과 대차거래 계약 전산 보고 체계, 그리고 KRX NSDS 간의 3중 검증망을 통해 무차입 공매도(Naked Short Selling)를 일 단위/실시간 수준으로 전수 점검하여 불법 공매도 시도를 원천 차단하고 있다.

기업 밸류업 프로그램 및 코리아 밸류업 지수 운용:

상장기업의 자발적 기업가치 제고 계획 공시와 연계된 ‘코리아 밸류업 지수’ ETF 및 밸류업 선물 상품이 기관·외국인 투자자의 핵심 벤치마크로 정착되어 코리아 디스카운트 해소에 기여하고 있다.

결제주기 T+1 전환 대응 및 분할결제 정착:

한국예탁결제원(KSD) 및 KRX는 글로벌 T+1 흐름에 발맞추어 결제대금 분할결제(2026년 4월부터 10억 원 단위 분할 차감)를 성공적으로 정착시켰으며, 2026년 10월 현재 국내 주식·채권 시장의 T+1 결제 전환 로드맵을 금융당국과 함께 구체화하고 있다.




4.2 북미 시장: T+1 결제 완전 정착 및 글로벌 24시간 거래(24/5) 상용화

DTCC/미국 시장 T+1 결제 안정화 2년 차 평가:

2024년 5월 28일 미국·캐나다·멕시코의 T+1 결제 전환 이후, 2026년 10월 현재 결제 실패율(Fail Rate)은 과거 T+2 시절 평균 수준 이하(2% 미만)로 완전히 안정화되었다.
DTCC의 당일 거래 매칭(Same-Day Affirmation) 비율이 95% 이상을 상시 유지하며, 청산소 증거금 부담 경감 효과가 연간 수십억 달러에 달하는 것으로 분석된다.

24시간 주식 거래소(24X National Exchange) 및 거래시간 연장 경쟁:

미국 SEC가 주 5일 24시간 거래를 표방하는 대체 거래 플랫폼(24X National Exchange 등)을 정식 승인함에 따라, NYSE(Pillar 플랫폼 22시간 거래 연장 계획 추진) 및 NASDAQ이 심야·새벽 시간대 글로벌 아시아/유럽 투자자를 겨냥한 연장 매매 인프라를 대폭 확장하고 있다.

미 국채(U.S. Treasury) 중앙청산 의무화 단계별 시행:

SEC 규정에 따른 FICC(DTCC 자회사)의 미국 국채 현물 및 레포(Repo) 시장 단계별 중앙청산 의무화가 2025년 말~2026년에 걸쳐 본격 적용되어, 글로벌 국채 거래의 카운터파티 리스크가 대폭 축소되었다.




4.3 유럽 시장: 2027년 10월 T+1 동시 전환 확정 및 DORA·EMIR 3.0 전면 발효

EU-영국-스위스 T+1 결제 2027년 10월 동시 전환 확정:

유럽연합(ESMA)과 영국(FCA/HM Treasury)은 파편화된 다국가 결제 환경의 혼선을 방지하기 위해 2027년 10월 둘째 주를 유럽 전역의 T+1 동시 라이브 시점으로 확정 발표하였으며, 2026년 10월 현재 전 금융기관 대상 통합 테스트 시나리오가 가동되고 있다.

DORA(디지털 운영 복원력법) 전면 시행 및 IT 감사 강화:

2025년 1월 17일 전면 발효된 DORA(Digital Operational Resilience Act)에 따라, 2026년 10월 현재 Euronext, Deutsche Börse, LSE 등 모든 역내 거래소 및 CCP는 AWS, Azure, Google Cloud 등 핵심 클라우드·ICT 제3자 서비스 제공업체(TPPs)에 대한 엄격한 장애 복원력 테스트(TLPT) 및 위험 관리 감사를 정례화하고 있다.

EMIR 3.0 및 Active Account Requirement (AAR) 규정 발효:

유로화 금리 스왑(IRS)의 런던 LCH 쏠림 현상을 완화하고 EU 역내 청산소(Eurex Clearing)의 전략적 자율성을 확보하기 위한 활성 계좌 요건(AAR)이 발효되어, Eurex Clearing의 장외파생 청산 점유율이 지속적으로 확대되고 있다.




4.4 아시아·태평양 시장: 거래시간 연장 정착 및 24/7 파생 인프라 경쟁

도쿄증권거래소(TSE/JPX) 15:30 연장 거래 및 종가 콜옥션 안정화:

2024년 11월 단행된 70년 만의 거래시간 30분 연장(15:00 → 15:30)과 5분간의 종가 콜옥션(Closing Auction) 제도가 2026년 10월 현재 완벽하게 정착되어, 종가 형성의 투명성과 장 마감 직전 유동성 집중 효과를 거두고 있다.

홍콩거래소(HKEX) 악천후 거래(Severe Weather Trading) 성공적 정착:

2024년 9월부터 태풍 8호 이상 경보나 흑색 폭우 경보 시에도 시장을 닫지 않고 정상 거래를 유지하는 전산망 비대면 재택 결제·매매 체계가 2026년 10월 현재 글로벌 표준으로 자리 잡았다.

인도(NSE/BSE) T+0 및 즉시결제 시스템 운용:

인도가 선도적으로 도입한 옵션형 T+0 결제 제도가 정착 단계에 진입하며, 글로벌 거래소들의 차세대 청산결제 아키텍처 벤치마킹 대상으로 부상하고 있다.

title: English Glossary — Global Exchange Research
text:
Derivatives








Term
Abbreviation
Definition




0DTE Options
0DTE
See: Zero Days to Expiration


ASX 24

ASX’s derivatives trading platform for futures and options on interest rates, equity indices, commodities, energy, and environmental products; formerly Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE); upgraded to New Trading Platform (NTP) in 2016; LSEG partnership announced March 2026 for further modernization (target H1 2028)


Automated Improvement Mechanism
AIM
Cboe’s electronic auction process allowing a member to seek price improvement for an agency order by exposing it to competing interest for a brief period (typically 1 second)


BAX

Three-Month Canadian Bankers’ Acceptance Futures — Montreal Exchange’s legacy short-term interest rate contract based on CDOR; open positions converted to CRA (CORRA futures) on April 26, 2024; formally discontinued after CDOR cessation on June 28, 2024


Block Trade

A privately negotiated, off-exchange transaction in listed futures or options that meets minimum size thresholds set by the exchange


Book or Cancel Order
BOC
An order that is rejected if it would immediately match upon entry, ensuring passive (maker) execution only; used at Eurex


Cancel on Disconnect
CoD
An optional feature that automatically cancels all working orders if the trading session is disconnected


Canadian Derivatives Clearing Corporation
CDCC
The central counterparty (CCP) for all exchange-traded derivatives on the Montreal Exchange and for a growing range of OTC instruments; wholly-owned subsidiary of Bourse de Montreal Inc.; designated as a systemically important FMI by the Bank of Canada; uses SPAN-based margin methodology since 1997


Cboe Futures Exchange
CFE
Cboe’s CFTC-regulated futures exchange, trading VIX futures, S&P 500 Variance futures, and other volatility products


Cboe Volatility Index
VIX
The market’s expectation of 30-day forward-looking volatility, calculated from S&P 500 (SPX) option prices; created in 1993, revised methodology in 2003; often called the “fear gauge”


Cheapest-to-Deliver
CTD
The deliverable bond that minimizes the cost for the short position holder in a physically-delivered futures contract, based on conversion factors and market conditions


Cloud Prisma Margin Estimator
cPME
Eurex’s web-based tool allowing participants to estimate margin requirements for hypothetical portfolios


CME Globex

CME Group’s electronic trading platform, first launched in 1992; the world’s first global electronic futures trading platform


Commitments of Traders
COT
CFTC weekly report publishing aggregated position data by trader category for U.S. futures markets


Conversion Factor
CF
A factor applied in physically-delivered bond futures to adjust for differences between the notional coupon and the actual coupon of the delivered bond


CORRA

Canadian Overnight Repo Rate Average — Bank of Canada’s preferred risk-free rate benchmark for CAD interest rate markets; replaced CDOR as the primary short-term interest rate benchmark; underlies Montreal Exchange’s CRA and COA futures contracts


Cross-Margining

The practice of recognizing risk offsets between correlated products or across different clearing organizations to reduce total margin requirements


CTP (Comprehensive Transaction Platform)
CTP
SHFE’s core electronic trading system, widely used across China’s futures industry; provides centralized order matching, risk management, and market data distribution; accessed via proprietary CTP API; primary data center at Zhangjiang, Shanghai


Designated Contract Market
DCM
A U.S. CFTC-registered exchange authorized to list futures and options contracts for trading


Derivatives Clearing Organization
DCO
A U.S. CFTC-registered clearinghouse that clears futures, options, and/or swaps


Dynamic Price Banding
DPB
HKEX’s pre-trade price validation mechanism that limits order prices to a band around the current best bid/ask, preventing erroneous orders from entering the order book


Eligible Contract Participant
ECP
A category of market participant under the Commodity Exchange Act eligible to trade certain off-exchange products (block trades, swaps)


Enhanced Trading Interface
ETI
Eurex’s high-performance native binary interface for T7, using FIX 5.0 SP2 semantics with proprietary session layer


Eurex EnLight

Eurex’s on-exchange selective Request-for-Quote (RFQ) platform with anonymous negotiation and STP integration


European Union Allowance
EUA
A tradable carbon emission permit under the EU Emissions Trading System; each EUA entitles the holder to emit one tonne of CO₂ equivalent; ICE Futures Europe is the primary trading venue


Exchange for Physical
EFP
A transaction involving the simultaneous exchange of a futures position for a corresponding physical commodity or forward contract


Exchange for Risk
EFR
A transaction involving the simultaneous exchange of a futures/options position for a corresponding OTC derivative


Exchange for Swap
EFS
A transaction involving the simultaneous exchange of a futures position for a corresponding OTC swap


Exchange of Options for Options
EOO
A transaction involving the simultaneous exchange of an OTC option for a listed option


EXTURE+

KRX’s unified electronic trading system launched in 2014, developed by KOSCOM; memory-based architecture on x86 Linux servers with ~30-50 microsecond latency and 100,000+ TPS; supports equities, bonds, futures, options, ETFs, and commodities


Extreme Loss Margin
ELM
An additional margin component applied by SEBI/NSE to cover tail risk beyond normal VaR-based margins; from November 2024, an additional 2% ELM is applied to short options positions on expiry day to address heightened volatility risk


Fill and Kill
FAK
An order that executes immediately for any available quantity, with unfilled portion cancelled (equivalent to IOC in some markets)


Futures Commission Merchant
FCM
A U.S.-registered entity that solicits or accepts orders for futures/options trading and accepts money or assets to margin such trades


GIFT City

Gujarat International Finance Tec-City — India’s international financial services centre (IFSC) at Gandhinagar, Gujarat; hosts NSE International Exchange (NSE IX), which operates GIFT Nifty (replacing SGX Nifty from July 2023) with ~19 hours/day trading coverage for international investors


Globex Credit Controls
GC2
CME’s exchange-provided GUI for clearing firms to set real-time, pre-execution risk limits per account


Historical Value-at-Risk
HVaR
A risk measurement methodology using historical market data scenarios to estimate potential portfolio losses; used in both SPAN 2 and Prisma


HKATS

Hong Kong Futures Automatic Trading System — HKEX’s electronic derivatives trading system, originally launched 1995, migrated to Nasdaq Genium INET platform in 2013


HKFE Clearing Corporation
HKCC
The clearing house for all products traded on HKFE (Hong Kong Futures Exchange), including index futures/options, currency futures, and commodity futures


ICE Risk Model
IRM
ICE’s proprietary risk methodology for margin calculation; IRM 2 (launched 2024-2025) uses Filtered Historical Simulation VaR at 99% confidence level, replacing the legacy scenario-based IRM


iLink 3

CME Group’s binary order entry protocol using FIX Simple Binary Encoding (SBE) with FIXP session layer


iMpact

ICE’s proprietary multicast market data protocol providing real-time depth-of-book data via UDP multicast for all ICE futures markets


Implied Pricing

The generation of synthetic orders from combinations of outright and spread orders, enhancing liquidity across related contracts


INE (Shanghai International Energy Exchange)
INE
SHFE’s wholly-owned subsidiary established 2013 for internationalized commodity futures; operates RMB-denominated contracts open to overseas traders including Crude Oil (SC, launched March 2018 — first mainland China commodity open to foreign participants), Low Sulfur Fuel Oil, TSR 20 Rubber, Bonded Copper, and Containerized Freight Index futures


Inline Credit Controls
ICC
CME’s granular, per-product, account-level daily position limits set by clearing members and executing firms


Inter-Commodity Spread Credit

A SPAN margin reduction recognizing risk offsets between correlated products (e.g., crude oil vs. heating oil)


Interval Price Limit
IPL
ICE’s dynamic circuit breaker mechanism that sets price bands around the last trade price; trading is paused temporarily if the limit is breached, then resumes with an expanded range


J-GATE

Osaka Exchange’s (OSE) derivatives trading system built on Nasdaq Genium INET technology; current version 3.0 launched September 2021; version 4.0 planned on Nasdaq Eqlipse platform (~2028)


J-NET

Osaka Exchange’s off-auction trading facility for negotiated large-lot derivative transactions at pre-agreed prices, analogous to block trade facilities at other exchanges


KOSPI 200 Options

Equity index options based on the KOSPI 200 index, traded on KRX since July 7, 1997; contract multiplier KRW 500,000 (quintupled from KRW 100,000 in June 2012); European-style cash-settled; historically the world’s most actively traded single derivatives contract (peak ~3.67 billion contracts in 2011)


KRX Night Trading Session

KRX’s independently operated after-hours derivatives trading session (18:00-06:00 KST), launched June 9, 2025, replacing the previous Eurex-linked arrangement; covers 10 products including KOSPI 200 futures/options, Mini products, KOSDAQ 150, USD futures, and KTB futures


KRX-SPAN

KRX’s modified SPAN-based margin methodology for listed derivatives; uses scenario-based portfolio risk assessment; includes intraday margin calls triggered when KOSPI 200 volatility reaches ≥80% of the futures margin rate


Lead Market Maker
LMM
A designated market participant required to provide continuous two-sided quotes with specific obligations; receives priority allocation in some matching algorithms


Liquidation Group

In Eurex Prisma, a grouping of products sharing similar risk characteristics for portfolio-based margin calculation; enables cross-margining between listed and OTC derivatives


Market with Protection

CME order type that executes within a pre-defined “protected range” from the current best price, preventing extreme fills; replaces traditional market orders on Globex


Market-Wide Position Limit
MWPL
In India’s derivatives markets, the maximum combined open interest (across all exchanges) permitted for a single underlying security; calculated as a percentage of the free-float market capitalization; when 95% of MWPL is breached, no new positions are allowed


Mass Quote

A message type allowing market makers to submit multiple two-sided quotes in a single message


MDP 3.0

CME Group’s market data platform using FIX SBE encoding over UDP multicast and TCP unicast


Negotiated Large Trade
NLT
SGX’s facility for privately negotiated off-order-book derivatives transactions that meet minimum volume thresholds; equivalent to block trades at other exchanges


NSE Clearing Limited
NCL
India’s first central counterparty (CCP) with settlement guarantee, formerly NSCCL (National Securities Clearing Corporation Limited); a wholly-owned subsidiary of NSE; provides novation, multilateral netting, and settlement guarantee for all trades on NSE’s equity, derivatives, currency, and commodity segments


Oman Marker Price

The daily benchmark price for DME/GME Oman Crude Oil Futures (OQD), determined during the Marker Window (16:25-16:30 Singapore Time) from trades on the front-month contract; used as the basis for Trade at Marker (TAM) transactions and serves as the official selling price benchmark for Oman and Dubai crude exports to Asia


OMD-D

HKEX’s Orion Market Data platform for the derivatives market, providing binary multicast data feeds for futures and options via UDP/IP


Peak Margin

SEBI’s margin rule (fully implemented September 2021) requiring 100% upfront margin collection for all intraday F&O positions in India; random snapshots taken 4-5 times daily to verify compliance; penalties for shortfall; a key component of SEBI’s retail investor protection framework


Performance Bond

CME’s term for margin — collateral required to cover potential future losses on open positions


Position Accountability

A threshold at which an exchange may contact a trader and request information about positions, but no hard limit applies


PRiME

Portfolio Risk Margining of Exchange Positions — HKCC’s margin methodology based on SPAN framework with a 1.33x client margin multiplier; evaluates 16 risk scenarios per product


Pro-Rata Matching

A matching algorithm where incoming quantity at each price level is allocated proportionally to resting order sizes rather than by time priority


Qualified Clearing Member Market Maker
QCMM
A type of HKEX derivatives market maker that is also a clearing member, required to provide continuous two-sided quotes with minimum size obligations in exchange for fee rebates


RiskGuard

Euronext’s pre-trade risk management service for derivatives and cash markets; provides order size limits, maximum order quantity, daily maximum exposure monitoring, kill switch functionality, and self-trade prevention via FIX 5.0 API and web-based GUI


SAIL (SOLA Access Information Language)
SAIL
Montreal Exchange’s native high-performance protocol for the SOLA trading platform; supports all order entry functionalities for brokers, HFT firms, and designated market makers


Scanning Range

In SPAN methodology, the maximum probable one-day price move for each product, used to generate risk scenarios


Sidecar (Derivatives Circuit Breaker)

KRX’s market-wide circuit breaker for derivatives; triggered when KOSPI 200 futures lead month hits ±5% of previous settlement for 1 minute with theoretical price variance ±3% or more; halts ALL derivatives contracts for 5 minutes


Self-Trade Prevention
STP
A configurable mechanism that prevents matching of orders from the same firm or account


SEOCH

The SEHK Options Clearing House Limited — HKEX’s clearing house for stock options traded on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong


SIMEX

Singapore International Monetary Exchange — Asia’s first financial futures exchange, established 1984; merged into SGX in 1999; pioneered mutual offset arrangement with CME for Eurodollar futures


SOLA

Montreal Exchange’s proprietary low-latency electronic trading engine developed in-house; median response time ~460 microseconds (post-2013 upgrade); messaging capacity 100,000+ quotes/second; also licensed to external venues including Boston Options Exchange (BOX); co-located at TMX Data Centre, Markham, Ontario


Special Opening Quotation
SOQ
The settlement calculation for equity index futures based on the opening prices of all constituent stocks on expiration day


Sponsored Access
SpA
A model allowing non-member entities to access exchange systems via an approved service provider without full exchange membership; introduced at Eurex T7 Release 14.0


Stop with Protection

CME order type that becomes a market-with-protection order when triggered, executing within the protected range


Systemically Important Financial Market Utility
SIFMU
A designation under the Dodd-Frank Act for FMUs whose failure could pose systemic risk; CME Clearing holds this designation


T+1 Session

TAIFEX’s after-hours trading session (15:00-05:00+1 TST) introduced May 2017, extending total trading coverage to ~19 hours/day for eligible equity index, foreign index, and commodity products; covers European and U.S. market hours; trades settle on the next business day


T7 Entry Services
TES
Eurex’s facility enabling off-book transactions (block trades, EFP, EFS) to be entered into the T7 system for standardized clearing


TMP (Transaction Messaging Protocol)
TMP
TAIFEX’s proprietary protocol for domestic participants to connect to the exchange’s electronic trading system; used alongside FIX protocol for international connectivity


TONA

Tokyo Overnight Average Rate — the Bank of Japan’s unsecured overnight call rate benchmark; OSE launched 3-Month TONA Futures in 2023, which have grown rapidly following BOJ rate hikes


Trade at Marker
TAM
DME/GME facility allowing market participants to execute trades at the daily Oman Marker Price; the marker is determined during the Marker Window (16:25-16:30 Singapore Time) from trades on the front-month OQD contract


Trade Price Validation
TPV
Euronext’s additional safeguard layer for derivatives markets that validates trade prices before execution to prevent aberrant trades; supplements the dynamic and static collar mechanisms


V-KOSPI 200

Volatility index measuring the implied volatility of KOSPI 200 options, analogous to the VIX; V-KOSPI 200 futures trade on KRX with a multiplier of KRW 250,000


Volatility Interruption
VI
Eurex’s circuit breaker mechanism that moves an instrument from continuous trading to a volatility auction when price deviation limits are breached


Volatility Interruption (VI) — KRX
VI
KRX’s dynamic circuit breaker mechanism consisting of Static VI (정적VI, triggered by deviation from previous settlement) and Dynamic VI (동적VI, triggered by ±3% deviation from recent reference price); triggers a 2-minute cooling-off period followed by single-price auction


Zero Days to Expiration
0DTE
Options contracts that expire on the same day they are traded; popularized by Cboe’s SPX daily expirations, reaching ~59% of SPX options volume in 2025

title: English Glossary — Global Exchange Research
text:
Trading








Term
Abbreviation
Definition




Add Liquidity Only Order
ALO
An order that is rejected rather than immediately executing, ensuring the sender always provides liquidity


Ask (Offer)

The lowest price at which a seller is willing to sell a security


Auction

A trading mechanism where orders are collected over a period and executed at a single price


Bid

The highest price at which a buyer is willing to buy a security


Circuit Breaker
CB
A mechanism that temporarily halts trading when prices move beyond predefined thresholds


Closing Auction

An auction held at the end of the trading day to determine the closing price


CONNEQTOR

JPX’s RFQ (Request for Quote) platform for ETF/ETN trading, enabling market makers to provide competitive quotes on demand


Consolidated Audit Trail
CAT
A comprehensive U.S. regulatory database tracking all equity and options order events across exchanges


Continuous Trading

A trading session where orders are matched immediately as they arrive against the order book


D-Order (D-Quote)

NYSE DMM discretionary order that allows price improvement during auctions and continuous trading


Dark Pool

A private trading venue that does not display orders publicly before execution


Designated Market Maker
DMM
A market participant assigned to specific securities on NYSE, responsible for maintaining fair and orderly markets (successor to the specialist role)


Designated Sponsor

Deutsche Borse/Xetra term for a contractually obligated liquidity provider who maintains continuous bid/ask quotes for less liquid securities to ensure tradability


Conditional Limit Order

KRX order type that acts as a limit order during continuous trading but converts to a market order at the closing call auction


Direct Market Access
DMA
Electronic trading infrastructure allowing buy-side firms to directly access exchange order books


Call Auction (Simultaneous Order Matching)

KRX’s single-price call auction mechanism (traditionally referred to as Simultaneous Bids and Offers or ‘Dongsi Hoga’) used for opening price, closing price, and VI-triggered auction price determination; all orders accumulated during the period are treated as arriving simultaneously and matched at a single equilibrium price.


Enhanced Limit Order
ELO
HKEX order type that can match up to 10 price queues beyond the best price on the opposite side


ETF Connect

Extension of the Stock Connect programme (launched July 2022) enabling cross-border trading of eligible ETFs between Hong Kong and mainland China exchanges


Forced Order Range
FOR
SGX mechanism that rejects orders priced beyond a specified range (e.g., +/-30 bids) from the current best price to prevent erroneous trades


Funari Order

JPX order type that acts as a limit order during continuous trading but converts to a market order at the closing auction


High-Frequency Trading
HFT
Automated trading strategy using high-speed systems to execute large numbers of orders in fractions of a second


Iceberg Order

An order type where only a portion of the total order quantity is visible in the order book


Intermarket Sweep Order
ISO
A limit order that simultaneously routes to multiple exchanges to sweep through protected quotes under Reg NMS


Itayose

JPX’s call auction method (板寄せ) used for opening/closing price determination, where orders are accumulated and matched at a single equilibrium price


Continuous Trading (Price-Time Priority)

KRX’s continuous trading method (traditionally termed ‘Jeopsokmaemae’) using price-time priority matching between opening and closing call auctions; standard continuous order book matching.


Limit Order

An order to buy or sell at a specified price or better


Limit Order Book
LOB
The collection of all outstanding limit orders for a given security


Limit Up-Limit Down
LULD
A U.S. price band mechanism that prevents trades outside specified percentage bands from a reference price


Lot Size

The minimum quantity of shares that can be traded in a standard transaction


Maker-Taker

A fee model where liquidity providers (makers) receive a rebate and liquidity takers pay a fee


Market Maker
MM
A firm that provides liquidity by continuously quoting bid and ask prices


Market Order

An order to buy or sell immediately at the best available price


Market-Wide Circuit Breaker
MWCB
A circuit breaker triggered by a decline in the S&P 500 index (7%/13%/20% thresholds) that halts all U.S. equity trading


Mid-Price Pegged Order
MPL
An order pegged to the midpoint of the NBBO, used for price improvement


National Best Bid and Offer
NBBO
The best available bid and ask price across all U.S. exchanges for a given security


Net Order Imbalance Indicator
NOII
Real-time data disseminated during NASDAQ opening/closing cross showing indicative prices and imbalances


Opening Auction

An auction held at the start of the trading day to determine the opening price


Order Book

An electronic list of buy and sell orders organized by price level


Parity Allocation

NYSE’s matching priority rule where orders at the same price share proportional fills among DMM, floor brokers, and displayed orders


Price-Time Priority

A matching rule where orders are first ranked by price, then by time of entry


Retail Price Improvement Order
RPI
A non-displayed order type on NYSE that provides price improvement to retail order flow


Market-Wide Circuit Breaker (KRX)
MWCB
KRX’s market-wide circuit breaker mechanism; triggers at KOSPI decline of -8% (Level 1, 20-min halt), -15% (Level 2, 20-min halt), and -20% (Level 3, trading terminated for the day); each level requires a 1-minute sustained duration confirmation before activation.


Self-Match Prevention
SMP
A mechanism that prevents orders from the same participant from matching against each other


Self-Regulatory Organization
SRO
An organization authorized to create and enforce rules governing its members (e.g., NYSE, NASDAQ, FINRA)


Sidecar (Program Trading Suspension)

KRX mechanism that suspends program trading orders for 5 minutes when KOSPI 200 front-month futures price moves +/-5% from base price for 1 minute; applied once per day, not after 14:50 KST


Special Quote (Tokubetsu Kehai)

JPX volatility interruption mechanism (特別気配) that temporarily halts continuous trading when price movement exceeds a threshold, displaying an indicative quote before resuming via Itayose auction


Stock Connect

Mutual market access program linking HKEX with Shanghai (2014) and Shenzhen (2016) stock exchanges, allowing cross-border equity trading


Stop Order

An order that becomes a market order when a specified price level is reached


Swap Connect

Mutual market access programme for interest rate swaps launched May 2023, linking HKEX’s OTC Clear with China Foreign Exchange Trade System (CFETS); world’s first derivatives mutual market access programme


Tick Size

The minimum price increment at which a security can be quoted or traded


Trading at Last
TAL
A post-closing-auction session (used by Euronext, SIX, BME, and others) where orders can execute only at the established closing price


Volatility Auction

A special auction triggered when price movements exceed certain thresholds


Volatility Control Mechanism
VCM
HKEX’s dynamic circuit breaker triggered when potential trades deviate +/-10% from a 5-minute reference price for designated securities, imposing a 5-minute cooling-off period


Volatility Interruption (KRX)
VI
KRX’s per-stock circuit breaker; Static VI triggers at 3% (KOSPI 200 constituents) or 6% (others) from last call auction price; Dynamic VI triggers at 10% from last trade price; activates a 2-minute call auction with random 30-second close


Zaraba

JPX’s continuous trading method (ザラバ) using price-time priority order matching between opening and closing auctions

title: English Glossary — Global Exchange Research
text:
Clearing








Term
Abbreviation
Definition




Anti-Procyclicality

Measures employed by CCPs to prevent margin requirements from dropping too low during calm periods and surging excessively during stress, thereby avoiding amplifying market volatility; required under PFMI and EMIR; approaches include using stressed lookback periods, margin floors, and buffers


Assessment Powers

The ability of a CCP to require additional contributions from clearing members beyond their default fund obligations


Back Testing

The process of comparing a CCP’s margin model predictions against actual realized market outcomes to assess model adequacy; CCPs are required under PFMI to back-test at least monthly and report coverage levels; typical target is 99% or higher coverage


CCP Recovery and Resolution Regulation
CCP RRR
EU regulation establishing a framework for the recovery and resolution of CCPs to ensure continuity of critical clearing functions; tools include VMGH, position allocation, cash calls, and partial tear-up


Central Counterparty
CCP
An entity that interposes itself between counterparties to trades, becoming the buyer to every seller and the seller to every buyer


Clearing Member
CM
A participant that is authorized to clear trades directly through a CCP


Close-out Netting

The termination of obligations under a contract with a defaulting party and the calculation of a single net amount


CME Clearing

CME Group’s clearing division providing CCP services for futures, options, and OTC derivatives across CME, CBOT, NYMEX, and COMEX; designated as a SIFMU; uses SPAN/SPAN 2 margin methodology; guaranty fund ~$10.1B


Concentration Margin

Additional margin charged when a clearing member’s positions are large relative to the market, reflecting liquidation risk


Concentration Risk

The risk that a clearing member or CCP has excessive exposure to a single counterparty, asset class, issuer, or market sector; CCPs mitigate this through concentration margin add-ons, position limits, and collateral diversification requirements


Continuous Net Settlement
CNS
NSCC’s core clearing process that nets all trades in the same security to a single deliver or receive obligation per participant per day


Cover 2

A CPMI-IOSCO standard requiring a CCP to maintain sufficient financial resources to cover the simultaneous default of its two largest clearing members under extreme but plausible market conditions


Cross-Guaranty Agreement

An arrangement between affiliated CCPs (e.g., NSCC-FICC-DTC-OCC) allowing cross-application of margin and default fund resources to cover losses from a defaulting member common to multiple CCPs


Default Fund
DF
A fund contributed to by clearing members to cover losses in the event of a member default


Default Waterfall

The sequence of financial resources used to cover losses resulting from a clearing member default


DTCC
DTCC
Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation — the holding company for DTC (depository/settlement), NSCC (equities clearing), and FICC (fixed income clearing); user-owned and industry-governed; processes approximately $3.7 quadrillion in securities transactions annually; designated as a SIFMU under Dodd-Frank Title VIII


DTC
DTC
Depository Trust Company — the CSD subsidiary of DTCC; holds over $100 trillion in assets under custody; provides book-entry settlement for U.S. equities, corporate bonds, and municipal securities


Eurex Clearing

Eurex Clearing AG — Europe’s largest CCP, subsidiary of Deutsche Börse Group; authorized under EMIR (2014); uses Prisma margin methodology; clears listed derivatives, OTC IRS, repos (GC Pooling), and securities lending; ~200 clearing members in 22 countries


Euronext Clearing

Euronext’s central counterparty (formerly CC&G / Cassa di Compensazione e Garanzia), headquartered in Rome; expanded to all Euronext financial derivatives markets in 2024, replacing LCH SA


EWMA
EWMA
Exponentially Weighted Moving Average — a statistical technique used in margin models to estimate volatility by assigning exponentially decreasing weights to older observations; commonly used in risk models to capture time-varying volatility dynamics


FICC
FICC
Fixed Income Clearing Corporation — DTCC subsidiary providing CCP clearing for U.S. government securities (GSD) and mortgage-backed securities (MBSD); GSD handles ~$13 trillion peak daily transaction value


Filtered Historical Simulation
FHS
A VaR estimation technique using historical data with volatility filtering; core methodology behind Eurex Clearing Prisma; uses 750 filtered historical + 250 stress scenarios


GC Pooling

Eurex Repo’s anonymous, CCP-cleared repo service using standardized collateral baskets; enables efficient secured funding with Eurex Clearing as CCP; record volumes of EUR 406B (2025)


General Clearing Member
GCM
A clearing member authorized to clear trades on behalf of itself and other market participants


Haircut

A percentage reduction applied to the market value of collateral (securities, cash in non-domestic currency) posted as margin, reflecting potential loss in value during liquidation; CCPs set haircut schedules based on asset type, credit quality, and liquidity


Individual Segregated Account
ISA
An account structure where a clearing member’s client positions and collateral are held separately at the CCP, providing full portability and protection in the event of the clearing member’s default


Initial Margin
IM
Collateral collected by a CCP from clearing members to cover potential future exposure


Interoperability

An arrangement allowing two or more CCPs to establish links so that participants of different CCPs can clear trades executed on the same trading venue; regulated under EMIR Article 51; implemented in European cash equities (e.g., Cboe Clear Europe, LCH, EuroCCP, SIX x-clear)


Joint Compensation Fund

KRX’s mutualized default fund for derivatives clearing; contributions from clearing members based on fixed + variable model; estimated size ~KRW 100 billion (~$75M); used after defaulter’s margin and clearing deposit are exhausted


LCH
LCH
London Clearing House — a multi-asset CCP majority owned by LSEG (82.61%); operates as LCH Ltd (London, regulated by Bank of England) and LCH SA (Paris, regulated by ACPR/Banque de France); clears OTC derivatives, repos, fixed income, FX, equities, and listed derivatives


Legal Entity Identifier
LEI
A 20-character alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies legal entities participating in financial transactions; mandated globally for derivatives trade reporting under EMIR, Dodd-Frank, and other regulations; issued by Local Operating Units under the Global LEI Foundation (GLEIF)


Lending CCP

Eurex Clearing’s securities lending service with CCP interposition, reducing counterparty risk in the securities lending market


Liquidity Add-on

An additional margin component charged by a CCP to account for the cost and risk of liquidating a defaulting member’s portfolio in illiquid markets; reflects bid-ask spreads, market depth, and position concentration


Loss Allocation

The process by which a CCP distributes uncovered losses (exceeding the default waterfall) among surviving clearing members; methods include VMGH, cash calls, forced allocation, and partial tear-up; governed by CCP rulebooks and the EU CCP RRR


Margin Period of Risk
MPOR
The time horizon assumed by a CCP for the close-out of a defaulting member’s positions; typically 2 days for exchange-traded derivatives, 5 days for OTC derivatives, and up to 10 days for client positions under EMIR; directly affects the level of initial margin collected


Multilateral Netting

The offsetting of obligations among multiple parties, resulting in a single net obligation for each participant


Netting Efficiency

The percentage reduction in gross settlement obligations achieved through multilateral netting; e.g., NSCC achieves ~98% netting efficiency, Cboe Clear Europe achieved 70.29% in 2024; higher netting efficiency reduces settlement risk and liquidity requirements


Novation

The process by which a CCP substitutes itself as the counterparty to both sides of a trade


NSCC
NSCC
National Securities Clearing Corporation — DTCC subsidiary providing CCP clearing, netting, and risk management for virtually all U.S. equities, corporate bonds, and ETF trades; achieves ~98% netting efficiency


OCC
OCC
Options Clearing Corporation — the world’s largest equity derivatives CCP, established 1973; jointly owned by Cboe, NYSE, NASDAQ exchanges; clears equity options, index options, futures, and securities lending; designated SIFMU; uses STANS margin methodology; 12.2B contracts cleared in 2024


Open Offer

A method of CCP interposition where the CCP becomes the counterparty to each side of a trade at the point of trade matching/execution, without an intervening bilateral contract between the original counterparties; used by Cboe Clear Europe, Muqassa, and LCH for exchange-traded products; contrasts with novation where a bilateral contract briefly exists before being replaced


PAIRS

Portfolio Approach to Interest Rate Scenarios — LCH SwapClear’s margin methodology; uses Expected Shortfall at 99.7% confidence level with a 5-day holding period and 10-year historical lookback including GFC floor scenarios


Partial Tear-Up

A CCP recovery tool allowing the termination of some (but not all) contracts of defaulted and/or non-defaulting members to allocate uncovered losses and restore a matched book


PFMI
PFMI
Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures — international standards issued by CPMI-IOSCO in 2012 for payment, clearing, and settlement systems; 24 principles covering governance, risk management, settlement, and transparency


Portfolio Margining

A margin methodology that evaluates risk at the portfolio level rather than position-by-position, recognizing offsets between correlated instruments; used by Eurex Clearing (Prisma), OCC (STANS), CME (SPAN 2), and LCH (PAIRS); can significantly reduce margin requirements compared to product-based margining


Porting

The transfer of a defaulting clearing member’s client positions and associated collateral to an alternative clearing member, enabling continuity of the client’s market exposure; portability depends on account segregation model (ISA provides full portability; omnibus/LSOC provides partial)


Prisma

Eurex Clearing’s portfolio-based margin methodology (Portfolio-based Risk management by Simulating scenario Matrices and Assessing market risks); uses filtered historical simulation with Expected Shortfall at 99%/99.5% confidence; enables cross-margining between listed and OTC products with up to 70% savings


Public Quantitative Disclosures
PQD
Standardized quarterly and annual disclosures by CCPs as recommended by CPMI-IOSCO; includes margin data, default fund sizes, stress test results, and back-testing coverage


Qualifying CCP
QCCP
A CCP that has been recognized as meeting international regulatory standards, resulting in lower capital requirements for its members


Security Token

A digital representation of a financial instrument (equity, bond, fund unit, or other security) issued and recorded on a distributed ledger (DLT/blockchain) under applicable securities law; in Korea, mandatory registration of all security tokens with KSD (Korea Securities Depository) is required under the revised Electronic Registration Act framework, effective January 2027


Recovery and Resolution

The framework for restoring a CCP to viability (recovery) or, if recovery fails, winding down in an orderly manner (resolution) while preserving critical clearing functions; governed by the EU CCP RRR, FSB Key Attributes, and CPMI-IOSCO Recovery Guidance; recovery tools include VMGH, cash calls, and partial tear-up; resolution tools include bridge CCP, mandatory tear-up, and public backstop


Settlement Facilitation Deposit

Collateral deposited by KRX clearing members to promote settlement completion; eligible collateral includes cash, government bonds, and monetary stabilization bonds


Skin in the Game
SITG
A CCP’s own financial resources contributed to the default waterfall, distinct from clearing member contributions


SIX x-clear

SIX Group’s CCP for equities and other instruments; planned consolidation with BME Clearing into a single multi-asset CCP headquartered in Madrid


SPAN
SPAN
Standard Portfolio Analysis of Risk — CME’s portfolio-based margin methodology using 16 risk scenarios analyzing price and volatility changes; widely adopted globally; being succeeded by SPAN 2 (HVaR + Expected Shortfall based)


SPAN 2

CME’s next-generation margin methodology replacing legacy SPAN; uses Historical Value-at-Risk with Expected Shortfall, full portfolio re-evaluation, and improved cross-product offsets; phased rollout 2023-2025


STANS
STANS
System for Theoretical Analysis and Numerical Simulations — OCC’s Monte Carlo-based margin methodology; uses full portfolio simulation with 10,000+ scenarios, Expected Shortfall at 99% confidence, 2-day holding period


Stress Testing

The process of evaluating a CCP’s financial resilience under extreme but plausible market scenarios, including the simultaneous default of the largest clearing members (Cover 2); required by PFMI, EMIR, and Dodd-Frank; CCPs must conduct stress tests at least daily and report results to regulators


Systemically Important Financial Market Utility
SIFMU
A designation under Dodd-Frank Title VIII for FMIs whose failure could create systemic risk; DTCC (DTC, NSCC, FICC), OCC, CME Clearing, and ICE Clear Credit are designated SIFMUs


Tear-Up

A CCP recovery or resolution tool involving the compulsory termination of contracts (both defaulted and non-defaulted) to restore a matched book and allocate losses; partial tear-up targets specific positions, while full tear-up terminates all contracts in a given clearing service


Trade Repository
TR
A centralized registry that maintains an electronic database of OTC derivative transaction records; mandated under EMIR, Dodd-Frank, and other G20 reforms to enhance transparency and enable regulatory monitoring of systemic risk; examples include DTCC Global Trade Repository, Regis-TR, and UnaVista


Variation Margin
VM
Daily (or intraday) payment to reflect current market value of open positions


Variation Margin Gain Haircutting
VMGH
A CCP recovery tool that reduces variation margin payments owed to members with mark-to-market gains to cover losses that exceed the default waterfall


Wrong-Way Risk

The risk that a clearing member’s exposure to the CCP increases at the same time as the member’s creditworthiness deteriorates; general wrong-way risk arises from correlation between exposure and counterparty credit quality; specific wrong-way risk occurs when exposure is directly linked to the counterparty (e.g., a member posting its own securities as collateral)

title: English Glossary — Global Exchange Research
text:
Settlement








Term
Abbreviation
Definition




BIS DVP Model 1

Gross-gross settlement — both securities and funds settle on a gross (trade-by-trade) basis simultaneously; provides the strongest settlement protection; used by T2S (Europe), Clearstream Europe, Euroclear Bank (Bridge)


BIS DVP Model 2

Gross securities, net funds — securities settle on a gross basis throughout the day, with a single net cash payment at the end of the day; used by some CSDs for government securities


BIS DVP Model 3

Net-net settlement — both securities and funds obligations are netted, with final net transfers occurring simultaneously; used by NSCC/DTC, HKSCC (CCASS CNS), CDP (Singapore)


Book-Entry

A method of recording ownership of securities electronically without physical certificates; transfers occur by debiting one account and crediting another on the books of a CSD or custodian


Buy-in

A mechanism requiring a buyer (or CCP) to purchase securities in the open market if the original seller fails to deliver within a specified period after the intended settlement date; may be mandatory (as originally proposed under CSDR) or voluntary; serves as a settlement discipline tool to address persistent settlement fails


Cash Penalty

A financial penalty imposed on participants who fail to settle on the intended settlement date; implemented under CSDR Settlement Discipline Regime in the EU since February 2022; penalty rates differ for equities, bonds, and SME Growth Market instruments


CCASS

Central Clearing and Settlement System — HKSCC’s integrated clearing, settlement, depository, and nominee services platform for Hong Kong securities; launched 1992; supports CNS netting, isolated trades, Stock Connect, and corporate actions


Central Securities Depository
CSD
An entity that holds securities in dematerialized form and enables transfer of securities through book entry


CHESS

Clearing House Electronic Subregister System — ASX’s electronic settlement and subregistry system for Australian equities, launched 1996; replacement project ongoing (DLT attempt abandoned 2022, TCS-based rebuild in progress)


Delivery versus Payment
DVP
A settlement mechanism that ensures delivery of securities occurs simultaneously with payment


Dematerialization

The elimination of physical securities certificates, replacing them entirely with electronic book-entry records at a CSD; most modern securities markets have fully dematerialized their securities


Iberclear

Spain’s central securities depository (CSD) for equities and fixed income; subsidiary of BME Group; migrated to TARGET2-Securities (T2S) platform in 2017


Immobilization

The practice of concentrating physical securities certificates in a central depository (CSD) and recording subsequent transfers through book entries, without eliminating the underlying physical certificates; contrasts with full dematerialization


International CSD
ICSD
A CSD that settles trades in international securities and various domestic securities (e.g., Euroclear, Clearstream)


JASDEC

Japan Securities Depository Center, Inc. — Japan’s central securities depository for equities and corporate bonds; provides book-entry transfer services for shares, investment trusts, corporate bonds, and commercial paper; operates under the Book-Entry Transfer Act


Korea Securities Depository (KSD)
KSD
South Korea’s central securities depository; established 1974; headquartered in Busan; provides securities custody, settlement agent services, fund settlement, and transfer agent services; ISO 20022 adopted; SWIFT BIC KSDCKRSEXXX; mandatory security token registration framework effective January 2027


Mandatory Buy-in

A mechanism requiring a buyer to purchase securities in the open market if the original seller fails to deliver within a specified period after the intended settlement date; proposed under CSDR but deferred in the EU; remains under discussion globally as a settlement discipline tool


Monte Titoli

Italian CSD for equities and other securities; subsidiary of Euronext (acquired with Borsa Italiana in 2021)


Omnibus Account

A single account held at a CSD that contains the securities of multiple underlying clients


Segregated Account

An account structure where each client’s securities are held separately


Settlement Cycle

The time period between trade date and settlement date (e.g., T+2)


Settlement Discipline Regime
SDR
CSDR provision imposing cash penalties on participants that fail to settle on the intended settlement date; mandatory buy-ins originally proposed but deferred


Settlement Finality

The point at which the transfer of securities and funds becomes irrevocable and unconditional


Settlement Finality Directive
SFD
EU Directive 98/26/EC providing legal certainty for settlement finality in designated payment and securities settlement systems, ensuring transfers cannot be unwound in insolvency


Split Settlement

KSD’s settlement system innovation introduced in 2021 that divides settlement into smaller units to reduce peak settlement risk; units progressively reduced from KRW 10 billion (2021) to 5 billion (2024) to 1 billion (April 2026)


Straight-Through Processing
STP
The automated end-to-end processing of trades without manual intervention


TARGET2-Securities
T2S
Eurosystem platform operated by the ECB providing a single pan-European platform for securities settlement in central bank money; used by Iberclear, Monte Titoli, and other European CSDs


Trade Date Affirmation

The process of confirming trade details between counterparties on trade date, critical for T+1 settlement; DTCC’s CTM platform targets same-day affirmation

title: English Glossary — Global Exchange Research
text:
Technology








Term
Abbreviation
Definition




arrowhead

JPX/TSE’s core trading system developed with Fujitsu; 4th generation launched November 2024 with ~0.2ms order response latency


arrownet

JPX’s dedicated high-speed network connecting market participants to the trading system and co-location facility


ASX Trade

ASX’s cash equities trading platform, powered by NASDAQ OMX Genium INET technology; replaced SEATS/ITS in 2010


ASX Trade24

Former name for ASX 24’s trading platform for futures and options; upgraded to New Trading Platform (NTP) in 2016; LSEG partnership announced March 2026 for next-generation modernization targeting H1 2028 go-live


Australian Liquidity Centre
ALC
ASX’s purpose-built data centre and co-location facility at Gore Hill Technology Park, Sydney; launched 2013; hosts over 100 financial institutions and service providers; provides lowest-latency access to ASX Trade and ASX 24 matching engines; carrier-neutral with IaaS offering


AutoCert+

CME Group’s mandatory automated certification tool for client systems using iLink 3 for Globex access


Binary Order Entry
BOE
Cboe’s native binary protocol for high-performance order entry; current version BOE v2/v3 provides lower latency than FIX


BOLT Plus

BSE’s (Bombay Stock Exchange) trading platform based on Deutsche Borse’s T7 architecture; launched for equity derivatives in November 2013 and extended to equity cash segment in April 2014


Bursa Trade Securities 2
BTS2
Bursa Malaysia’s securities trading platform powered by Nasdaq’s X-Stream INET technology; launched December 2013, replacing the NYSE Technologies NSC engine


Canton Network

A privacy-enabled interoperable blockchain network for institutional assets; DTCC, in partnership with major financial institutions, is developing tokenization of DTC-custodied U.S. Treasury securities on the Canton Network; SEC issued a No-Action Letter in December 2025 authorizing DTC’s participation; MVP planned for H1 2026


Cboe Titanium

Cboe’s proprietary trading technology platform, evolved from BATS technology after the 2017 acquisition; powers all Cboe U.S. equities and options exchanges


Co-location
Colo
Hosting trading infrastructure in the same data center as the exchange’s matching engine


D7

The Bank of England’s Digital Securities Depository programme; aims to create a digital securities depository for UK government bonds (gilts) using DLT technology; part of the UK’s broader initiative to modernize post-trade infrastructure


DCASS

Derivatives Clearing and Settlement System — HKCC/SEOCH’s clearing platform, migrated to Nasdaq Genium INET in 2013; handles margin calculation, position management, and settlement


EMDI
EMDI
Eurex’s Enhanced Market Data Interface — un-netted feed disseminating every order book change and on-exchange trades via multicast


EOBI
EOBI
Eurex’s Enhanced Order Book Interface — full order book (L3) data with individual order details; ultra-low latency for co-located participants


Eqlipse

NASDAQ’s fourth-generation marketplace technology platform, launched 2024; successor to previous Nasdaq INET generations


EXTURE

Korea Exchange’s first unified electronic trading platform, launched March 2009; consolidated three legacy exchange systems (KSE, KOSDAQ, KOFEX); ~20 ms latency; 250 TPS; replaced by EXTURE+ in 2014


EXTURE+

Korea Exchange’s second-generation unified trading platform, launched 2014; first Linux x86 deployment in Korean capital markets; <=70 us worst-case latency; 20,000+ TPS matching; 100,000+ TPS throughput; replaced by Exture 3.0 in 2023


Exture 3.0

Korea Exchange’s current integrated trading, information distribution, clearing, and settlement platform; Phase 1 launched January 2023 (trading), Phase 2 October 2023 (clearing/settlement); ~30% latency improvement over EXTURE+; extended low-latency to entire system


Equinox

SIX Swiss Exchange’s next-generation trading platform; equity go-live targeted for H1 2027, replacing the current X-stream INET (SWXess) system


FAST Protocol
FAST
FIX Adapted for Streaming — a data compression protocol for market data


FAST System (TWSE)
FAST
Fully Automated Securities Trading system — TWSE’s core trading platform; 2nd generation (2014) provides <3ms latency and 20 million transactions/day capacity


FIX Protocol
FIX
Financial Information eXchange — a standard electronic communications protocol for trading


FLEX (Full Line-speed Exchange)
FLEX
JPX’s market data feed protocol providing Standard, MBO (Market by Order), and MBO BC (Broadcast) data streams


FPGA
FPGA
Field-Programmable Gate Array — hardware used for ultra-low-latency trading


FpML
FpML
Financial products Markup Language — an XML-based open standard for electronic dealing and processing of OTC derivatives; maintained by ISDA; widely used for trade confirmation, reporting, and lifecycle management of swaps, options, and structured products


Genium INET

Nasdaq’s trading technology platform used by multiple exchanges globally including HKEX (derivatives), SGX, ASX, SIX, and Tadawul; offers sub-millisecond latency matching


GIFT Connect

SGX-NSE IX mutual market access program (operational July 2023) enabling cross-border trading of Indian derivatives through Singapore


Group Ticker Plant
GTP
LSEG’s aggregated market data distribution system that normalizes data across venues with intelligent throttling


ICE Trading Platform

ICE’s proprietary electronic trading platform providing global connectivity across all ICE futures markets; data centers in Chicago (IFUS), Basildon/London (IFEU), and Mahwah (DR)


Iris-ST

SGX’s next-generation securities trading engine, planned for launch in H2 2027


ISO 15022

An international standard for securities messaging using the SWIFT MT message format; the legacy standard for securities settlement, corporate actions, and custody messaging; being replaced by ISO 20022


ISO 20022

An international standard for electronic data interchange between financial institutions; uses XML/ASN.1-based messaging with rich, structured data; adopted by SWIFT (migration from MT to MX messages), T2S, CDP Singapore (Phase 1, 2016), and increasingly mandated for payment and securities infrastructure globally


ITCH Protocol
ITCH
A direct data feed protocol that provides full depth-of-book data (used by NASDAQ and others)


Matching Engine
ME
The core component of a trading system that matches buy and sell orders


KOSCOM (Korea Securities Computing Corporation)

Korea’s financial IT infrastructure provider; primary technology partner for KRX; develops and operates EXTURE/EXTURE+/Exture 3.0 trading systems; distributes KRX market data via STOCK-NET dedicated financial network


Millennium Advanced Platform
MAP
LSEG Technology’s integrated multi-asset offering bundling Millennium Exchange, Surveillance, and Post-Trade modules; deployed at 40+ markets globally


Millennium Exchange

LSE’s trading platform launched in 2011, built on C++/Linux for low-latency matching; developed by MillenniumIT (Sri Lanka); deployed across 40+ financial markets worldwide including JSE (2012)


MillenniumIT

LSEG subsidiary based in Colombo, Sri Lanka; founded 1996 by Tony Weerasinghe; acquired by LSEG in 2009 for GBP 18M; develops Millennium Exchange and related trading technology


MITCH Protocol
MITCH
LSE’s native market data protocol providing real-time Level 1 and Level 2 data via UDP multicast


MoldUDP64

NASDAQ’s transport protocol for reliable multicast delivery of market data messages


NEAT / NEAT Plus

National Exchange for Automated Trading — NSE India’s in-house developed trading system; India’s first screen-based electronic trading platform (launched 1994); NEAT Plus provides a unified multi-market interface across equity, derivatives, currency, and commodity segments; current system handles ~5-6 million transactions/second with ~100 microsecond latency; nanosecond-level upgrade planned from April 2026 targeting 100 million transactions/second


NTP (New Trading Platform)
NTP
ASX’s upgraded derivatives trading platform for ASX 24, launched 2016; handles interest rate, equity index, commodity, energy, and environmental futures and options; announced March 2026 partnership with LSEG for further modernization


OAPI

Open Application Programming Interface — HKEX’s proprietary API for derivatives trading, providing order entry and market data access to HKATS


OMD-C

HKEX’s Orion Market Data platform for the securities market, providing binary multicast data feeds via UDP/IP


Optiq

Euronext’s proprietary trading platform for cash and derivatives markets; deployed across all Euronext venues (Amsterdam, Brussels, Dublin, Lisbon, Milan, Oslo, Paris, Athens); Borsa Italiana migration completed in three phases (2023-2024)


Orion Trading Platform
OTP-C
HKEX’s current securities trading platform launched February 2018, supporting 60,000 orders/second capacity


OUCH Protocol
OUCH
A simplified order entry protocol used by NASDAQ and other exchanges


Pillar

NYSE’s modern trading technology platform, providing a single integrated system across all NYSE equity and options exchanges


PITCH Protocol
PITCH
Cboe’s native market data protocol providing full depth-of-book data (Level 3) via multicast; originally developed by BATS


Project Ion

DTCC’s DLT-based settlement platform for U.S. equities; went live in parallel production in 2022, processing 100,000+ equity transactions daily; demonstrates alternative settlement using distributed ledger technology alongside the existing DTC infrastructure


SDNet

HKEX’s Securities and Derivatives Network providing connectivity between participants and HKEX systems; SDNet/3 is the latest generation


SGX REACH

SGX’s securities trading platform based on Nasdaq technology


SIBE

Sistema de Interconexion Bursatil Espanol — BME’s electronic trading platform connecting the four Spanish stock exchanges (Madrid, Barcelona, Bilbao, Valencia); launched 1995; SIBE-Smart upgrade in 2012 reduced latency by more than 10x


SIX Digital Exchange
SDX
SIX Group’s fully regulated digital asset exchange and CSD; received FINMA license in 2019; began live operations in 2021; world’s first regulated digital securities exchange


SoupBinTCP

A framing protocol used for reliable, session-based TCP delivery of NASDAQ data feeds


STOCK-NET

KOSCOM’s dedicated high-speed financial network connecting KRX, securities/futures firms, KOFIA, and institutional investors for real-time market data distribution and trading connectivity


SwissAtMid

SIX Swiss Exchange’s non-displayed (dark) liquidity pool, launched 2018; provides midpoint matching for institutional block orders


T7

Deutsche Borse Group’s high-performance trading platform; used for Xetra equities (launched June 2017) and Eurex derivatives; also the basis for BSE’s BOLT Plus platform


Titan

SGX’s derivatives trading platform based on Nasdaq technology, providing sub-100 microsecond latency


TMX Quantum XA

TMX Group’s proprietary trading platform; rolled out across TSX, TSXV, and TSX Alpha Exchange in 2013-2014


ToSTNeT

JPX’s off-auction trading system (Tokyo Stock Exchange Trading NeTwork) for large-lot and basket trades executed at pre-agreed prices


TradElect

LSE’s former trading platform (2007-2011) built on Microsoft .NET; replaced by Millennium Exchange due to latency and reliability issues


X-Stream INET

Nasdaq’s trading technology deployed at multiple exchanges; used by Tadawul (2015), SIX Swiss Exchange (2012, branded SWXess), and Bursa Malaysia (2013)


XDP
XDP
NYSE’s Exchange Data Publisher — a low-latency market data feed for real-time depth-of-book data

title: English Glossary — Global Exchange Research
text:
Market Segments & Boards








Term
Abbreviation
Definition




AIM (Alternative Investment Market)
AIM
LSE’s international growth market for smaller and emerging companies; classified as an MTF under MiFID II; no minimum market cap; requires a Nominated Adviser (Nomad)


AltX (Alternative Exchange)
AltX
JSE’s parallel market for small and medium-sized high-growth companies; launched 2003; requires a Designated Adviser


BME Growth

BME’s Multilateral Trading Facility for SMEs (formerly Mercado Alternativo Bursatil / MAB); renamed 2020; requires a Registered Adviser (Asesor Registrado)


Catalist

SGX’s sponsor-supervised growth board for SMEs and high-potential startups; no quantitative entry criteria set by SGX; Full Sponsor determines suitability


ChiNext

SZSE’s NASDAQ-style board (创业板) for innovative, high-growth enterprises launched October 2009; registration-based IPO system since August 2020; +/-20% daily price limit


Euronext Access / Access+

Euronext’s entry-level MTF for start-ups and SMEs; Access+ is a special compartment for fast-growing SMEs acting as a springboard to Euronext Growth


Euronext Growth

Euronext’s SME Growth Market (MTF under MiFID II) for small and mid-sized companies; operates across all Euronext markets; requires a Listing Sponsor


Euronext Growth Milan

Formerly AIM Italia; MTF for Italian SMEs under Euronext ownership; requires an Euronext Growth Advisor (formerly Nomad)


Euronext STAR Milan

Segment within Euronext Milan for mid-cap companies committing to higher transparency, governance, and liquidity standards; ~61 companies


First North Growth Market

Nasdaq Nordic’s MTF for smaller/growth companies across Sweden, Finland, Denmark, Iceland, and the Baltic states; licensed as an SME Growth Market under MiFID II; requires a Certified Adviser


GEM (Growth Enterprise Market)
GEM
HKEX’s market for smaller, high-growth companies with less stringent requirements than the Main Board


KONEX (Korea New Exchange)

KRX’s third-tier market for startups and SMEs, launched July 2013; serves as a pre-KOSDAQ stage for early-stage companies; ~129 listed companies as of January 2024; viability questioned due to low new listing activity


KOSDAQ

KRX’s growth market for technology and venture companies, launched 1996; ~1,700+ listed companies; Korean equivalent of NASDAQ


KOSPI (Korea Composite Stock Price Index)

KRX’s main board equities market; ~954 listed companies; blue-chip large-cap market; also refers to the benchmark price index


Latibex

BME’s international market for Latin American securities traded in euros; launched 2001; provides European investors access to LatAm companies


Nomu (Parallel Market)

Saudi Exchange’s parallel market for SME listings launched February 2017; lighter listing requirements than the Main Market (TASI); Arabic for “growth”


Nextrade (NXT)

South Korea’s first alternative exchange, launched March 2025; operates 12-hour trading sessions (08:00-20:00 KST); ended KRX’s monopoly as sole securities exchange operator; captured 30%+ market share by July 2025


NSE EMERGE

NSE India’s platform for SME IPOs and secondary market trading; launched 2012


Scale

Deutsche Borse’s growth segment within the Open Market (Freiverkehr) for small and mid-cap companies; requires a Designated Sponsor


Sparks

SIX Swiss Exchange’s dedicated segment for SMEs launched October 2021; companies must have market cap below CHF 500 million


STAR Market

SSE’s Science and Technology Innovation Board (科创板, Kechuangban) launched June 2019; first Chinese board with registration-based IPO system; +/-20% daily price limit; focus on new materials, new energy, biomedicine, IT, high-end equipment, environmental tech


TOKYO PRO Market

JPX/TSE’s professional investors market launched 2009; flexible listing criteria targeting qualified institutional investors; requires a J-Adviser

title: English Glossary — Global Exchange Research
text:
Regulation








Term
Abbreviation
Definition




Australian Securities and Investments Commission
ASIC
Australia’s primary market conduct regulator for securities, derivatives, and financial services


Autorite des marches financiers (Quebec)
AMF
Quebec’s financial markets regulator; lead regulator for the Montreal Exchange (MX) and CDCC; grants recognized exchange and self-regulatory organization (SRO) status under Quebec’s Derivatives Act


Best Execution

The obligation to execute client orders on the most favorable terms available


Bundesanstalt fur Finanzdienstleistungsaufsicht
BaFin
Germany’s federal financial supervisory authority overseeing banking, insurance, and securities


Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization
CIRO
Canada’s national self-regulatory organization formed in 2023 from the merger of IIROC and MFDA; administers Universal Market Integrity Rules (UMIR)


Capital Market Authority (Saudi Arabia)
CMA
Saudi Arabia’s securities regulator established 2003 under the Capital Market Law; oversaw progressive foreign investor liberalization


CEA (Commodity Exchange Act)
CEA
U.S. federal law governing the trading of commodity futures and options


CFTC
CFTC
Commodity Futures Trading Commission — U.S. independent agency regulating commodity futures, options, and swaps markets


China Securities Regulatory Commission
CSRC
China’s central regulatory authority managing SSE, SZSE, and BSE; oversees the registration-based IPO system


College of Euronext Regulators

Coordinating body of national regulators (AMF, AFM, FSMA, CMVM, CBI, Finanstilsynet, CONSOB, HCMC) overseeing Euronext’s multi-jurisdictional operations


CONSOB

Commissione Nazionale per le Societa e la Borsa — Italy’s securities market regulatory authority


Consolidated Tape Provider
CTP
An entity authorized to aggregate and publish post-trade data across all trading venues (EU concept under MiFID II/MiFIR)


Corporate Governance Code

Japan’s principles-based framework for listed companies’ governance practices, administered by TSE (first issued 2015, revised periodically)


CPMI-IOSCO

Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures / International Organization of Securities Commissions


CSDR
CSDR
Central Securities Depositories Regulation — EU regulation on settlement discipline, CSD authorization, and buy-in rules


Digital Operational Resilience Act
DORA
EU regulation requiring financial entities and ICT third-party providers to meet operational resilience standards (applied January 2025)


Dodd-Frank Title VII

Title VII of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (2010); establishes a comprehensive regulatory framework for OTC derivatives including mandatory clearing of standardized swaps through registered DCOs, swap execution facility (SEF) trading, and trade reporting


Dodd-Frank Title VIII

Title VIII of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (2010); provides for enhanced regulation and supervision of Systemically Important Financial Market Utilities (SIFMUs) by the Federal Reserve Board; DTCC, OCC, CME Clearing, and ICE Clear Credit are designated SIFMUs


Double Volume Cap / Single Volume Cap
DVC / SVC
MiFID II mechanism limiting dark pool trading as a percentage of total volume; reformed from dual cap (4%/8%) to single 7% cap under MiFIR Refit


Dubai Financial Services Authority
DFSA
The independent regulator of the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC); supervises DME/GME as a licensed exchange operating within the DIFC financial free zone; maintains cooperation agreements with international regulators


EMIR
EMIR
European Market Infrastructure Regulation — EU regulation on OTC derivatives, CCPs, and trade repositories


Electronic Securities Act

South Korea’s Act on Electronic Registration of Stocks, Bonds, etc. (주식·사채 등의 전자등록에 관한 법률); governs the electronic registration of securities at KSD and designated registrars; revisions extended the framework to cover security tokens, with mandatory KSD registration of all security tokens effective January 2027


ESMA
ESMA
European Securities and Markets Authority — EU supervisory authority coordinating securities regulation across member states


Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act (FSCMA)
FSCMA
South Korea’s primary securities law; function-based regulation covering stocks, bonds, collective investment schemes, and derivatives; administered by FSC/FSS


Financial Instruments and Exchange Act
FIEA
Japan’s primary securities regulation law, governing securities trading, disclosure, and market conduct


Financial Market Infrastructure Act
FMIA
Switzerland’s primary legislation governing financial market infrastructures, including exchanges, CCPs, CSDs, and trade repositories; administered by FINMA


Financial Services Commission (Korea)
FSC (금융위원회)
South Korea’s highest financial regulatory authority; formulates policy, licensing, and approval of financial companies; supervises KRX


Financial Sector Conduct Authority
FSCA
South Africa’s primary market conduct regulator for the financial sector, including oversight of the JSE


Financial Supervisory Service (Korea)
FSS (금융감독원)
FSC’s enforcement arm in South Korea; conducts examinations, investigations, and sanctions across all financial sectors


Financial Services and Markets Act
FSMA
UK primary legislation governing financial services regulation


Financial Supervisory Commission (Taiwan)
FSC
Taiwan’s consolidated financial regulatory authority overseeing banking, securities, futures, and insurance markets; supervises TAIFEX as the sole licensed futures exchange and derivatives clearing house in Taiwan


FINMA
FINMA
Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority — Switzerland’s integrated financial market regulator


FINRA
FINRA
Financial Industry Regulatory Authority — U.S. SRO overseeing broker-dealers, market integrity, and investor protection


Futures and Derivatives Law (China)

China’s first comprehensive law on futures and derivatives, effective August 1, 2022; provides legal foundation for futures market development, investor protection, cross-border activities, and the QFI access scheme; enacted by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress


Futures Trading Law (Taiwan)

Taiwan’s primary legislation governing the domestic futures market, enacted 1997; established the legal framework for domestic futures exchanges, futures commission merchants, clearing, and trading; authorized the creation of TAIFEX


Japan Financial Services Agency
JFSA
Japan’s primary financial regulatory authority overseeing banking, securities, and insurance sectors


JPX-R (Japan Exchange Regulation)
JPX-R
JPX’s self-regulatory organization responsible for listing examination, market surveillance, and compliance


Living Will (CCP)

A resolution plan prepared by or for a CCP describing how it could be resolved in an orderly manner in the event that recovery measures fail; required under the EU CCP Recovery and Resolution Regulation (EU 2021/23) and recommended by FSB Key Attributes


Market Abuse Regulation
MAR
EU/UK regulation prohibiting insider dealing, market manipulation, and unlawful disclosure of inside information


MiFID II / MiFIR

Markets in Financial Instruments Directive II / Regulation — EU regulatory framework for financial markets


Monetary Authority of Singapore
MAS
Singapore’s central bank and integrated financial regulator


Multilateral Trading Facility
MTF
An EU-regulated trading venue operated by an investment firm or market operator matching buy/sell interests (alternative to regulated market)


No Creditor Worse Off
NCWO
A fundamental principle of resolution regimes requiring that no creditor of a failed institution should be left worse off than they would have been under normal insolvency proceedings; applied to CCP resolution under the EU CCP RRR and FSB Key Attributes


Organised Trading Facility
OTF
An EU trading venue category under MiFID II for non-equity instruments, with operator discretion in execution


PFMI
PFMI
Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures — international standards for FMIs issued by CPMI-IOSCO


Qualified Foreign Investor
QFI
Unified scheme (replacing QFII and RQFII) for foreign institutional access to China’s A-share markets; quota limits abolished in 2020


QFII / RQFII

Qualified Foreign Institutional Investor / RMB Qualified Foreign Institutional Investor — legacy schemes (introduced 2002/2011) for foreign institutional access to China’s securities markets; merged into unified QFI scheme in 2020


Registration-Based IPO System

China’s reformed IPO mechanism replacing the approval-based system; first piloted on STAR Market (2019), then ChiNext (2020), fully rolled out across all boards (2023); shifts from merit-based government approval to disclosure-based registration


Regulation ATS
Reg ATS
U.S. SEC regulation governing alternative trading systems (dark pools, ECNs)


Regulation NMS
Reg NMS
Regulation National Market System — U.S. SEC regulation governing equity market structure


Regulation SHO
Reg SHO
U.S. SEC regulation governing short selling, including locate requirements and close-out obligations


Rule 17Ad-22

SEC rule establishing standards for covered clearing agencies (CCPs/CSDs) in the United States; Rule 17Ad-22(e) (effective April 2017) implements PFMI-based enhanced standards for SIFMUs including NSCC, DTC, FICC, OCC, and ICE Clear Credit; covers governance, risk management, margin, default procedures, and operational risk


Securities and Exchange Board of India
SEBI
India’s primary securities regulatory authority overseeing NSE, BSE, and other market participants


Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission
SESC
Japan’s market surveillance body responsible for investigating insider trading, market manipulation, and other violations


Securities and Futures Act
SFA
Singapore’s primary legislation governing securities, futures, and financial advisers (enacted 2001)


Securities and Futures Commission
SFC
Hong Kong’s statutory regulatory body overseeing the securities and futures markets


Securities Commission Malaysia
SC
Malaysia’s primary securities regulatory authority overseeing Bursa Malaysia and capital market activities


Securities Information Processor
SIP
U.S. consolidated data feed aggregating quotes and trades from all exchanges into a single stream (CTS/CQS for Tapes A/B, UTP for Tape C)


SGX RegCo

SGX’s independent regulatory subsidiary responsible for listing regulation, market surveillance, and enforcement


Short Selling Regulation
SSR
EU regulation requiring disclosure of net short positions and restricting uncovered short selling


SIX Exchange Regulation
SER
SIX Swiss Exchange’s self-regulatory body handling listing and trading rule supervision


Systematic Internaliser
SI
An investment firm that executes client orders against its own account on a regular and systematic basis outside a trading venue (MiFID II concept)


Systematically Important FMI
SI-FMI
An FMI whose failure could pose systemic risk to the financial system


Universal Market Integrity Rules
UMIR
Canadian rules governing equity trading conduct, administered by CIRO; cover topics including best execution, short selling, and market manipulation
