title: Global Derivatives Markets — Overview
text:
3. Market Structure

3.1 Exchange-Traded vs OTC
The global derivatives market spans both exchange-traded derivatives (ETD) and over-the-counter (OTC) markets:

ETD markets reached ~205 billion contracts in 2024, dominated by equity options (~86% of volume)
OTC notional outstanding exceeded $700 trillion (end-2024), dominated by interest rate derivatives (~$548T)
Post-2008 regulatory mandates (Dodd-Frank, EMIR) have pushed standardized OTC derivatives toward central clearing, blurring the line between exchange-traded and OTC markets
Major CCPs now clear both ETD and OTC products (e.g., CME Clearing, Eurex Clearing, ASX Clear Futures, LCH)



3.2 Trading Mechanisms








Mechanism
Description
Examples




Electronic order book (CLOB)
Continuous matching via price-time priority; dominant mechanism globally
CME Globex, Eurex T7, Optiq, SOLA, ASX 24, HKATS, J-GATE, Titan, Cboe Titanium


Request for Quote (RFQ)
Electronic negotiation for less liquid instruments; market makers provide competitive quotes
Eurex EnLight, ICE, HKEX, Cboe AIM


Block trading / negotiated trades
Off-book large-lot transactions at pre-agreed prices, reported to exchange for clearing
All major exchanges (e.g., CME EFP/EFS/EOO, Eurex TES, OSE J-NET, SGX NLT, ASX Custom Market)


Trade at Marker (TAM)
Execution at a published daily marker price
DME/GME (Oman Marker Price)





3.3 Market Participants

Hedgers: Commercial entities managing commodity, interest rate, FX, and equity risk
Speculators: Including retail investors (particularly dominant in India’s options market), hedge funds, and proprietary firms
Arbitrageurs: Exploiting price discrepancies across related contracts and venues
Proprietary trading firms / HFT: High-speed algorithmic market makers providing liquidity
Market makers: Exchange-designated liquidity providers with quoting obligations and incentives

Key Observations: - The industry is converging toward VaR-based methodologies (SPAN 2, Prisma, IRM 2) that use historical simulation with thousands of scenarios, replacing SPAN’s fixed 16-scenario framework - Chinese exchanges (CFFEX, DCE, SHFE) remain on fixed-percentage systems with extensive regulatory discretion to adjust margins during volatile periods or holidays - Cross-margining across products is increasingly available at CME, Eurex, and other multi-asset CCPs - Anti-procyclicality measures (stress VaR floors, volatility buffers) are now standard at major CCPs

title: Global Derivatives Markets — Overview
text:
6. Key Trends

6.1 Explosion of Options Trading & Retail Participation

Global options volume reached 177 billion contracts in 2024 (+63.8% YoY), now ~86% of all ETD volume
NSE India alone traded ~92-108 billion contracts in 2024 (mostly equity options), driven by massive retail participation
SEBI’s September 2024 study revealed 93% of individual F&O traders incurred losses between FY22-FY24, leading to comprehensive regulatory curbs
Post-SEBI curbs (November 2024), NSE volumes declined ~30-38%, and B3 overtook NSE as #1 globally in H1 2025



6.2 0DTE (Zero Days to Expiration) Options Revolution

0DTE options averaged 14 million contracts/day in 2025, up 41% YoY
0DTE accounted for 24.1% of all U.S. listed options volume in 2025 (up from 21.5% in 2024, nearly double the 2022 share)
SPX 0DTE contracts became the most traded S&P 500 options, surpassing all other expiration dates combined in Q4 2024
Cboe’s daily SPX expirations (launched 2022) were the catalyst; 0DTE reached ~59% of SPX options volume by 2025
Both retail (50% of options volume via retail broker flows) and institutional participants are adopting 0DTE strategies



6.3 Micro/Nano Contracts for Retail Access

CME Micro E-mini suite (S&P 500, Nasdaq, Gold, Crude) continues to grow, lowering capital requirements for retail
TAIFEX launched Micro TAIEX Futures; ASX offers Mini SPI 200
DME/GME launched Micro Oman Crude Oil Futures (100 barrels vs. standard 1,000)
Euronext introduced mini single stock options (May 2025) and mini ETF options (March 2026)



6.4 ESG & Environmental Derivatives

ICE environmental markets saw a record 20.9 million contracts in 2025 (+4% YoY)
EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) allowances remain the most liquid environmental derivative (ICE Futures Europe primary venue)
ASX lists ACCU (Australian Carbon Credit Unit) Futures, NZU Futures, and LGC Futures
Euronext launched CAC 40 ESG index futures
Global carbon market exceeded $1 trillion in 2025
Renewable energy carbon credit market exceeded USD 43.3 billion in 2024



6.5 Cryptocurrency Derivatives

Crypto derivatives market expanded to $8.94 trillion monthly in 2025
CME Bitcoin and Ether futures/options continue to grow as regulated venues
Average daily volume in Ether options grew 65% from 2024 to 2025
Bitcoin and Ethereum together account for ~68% of crypto derivatives volume



6.6 Extended Trading Hours

TAIFEX offers 19-hour coverage (day + after-hours T+1 session since 2017)
ASX 24 provides near-24-hour trading for interest rate and equity index futures
CME Globex offers ~23 hours/day across asset classes
SHFE/DCE/CFFEX night sessions extend coverage to overlap with London and New York
Euronext extended equity index futures hours to 22:00 CET (covering U.S. session)
KRX launched independent night session (18:00-06:00 KST) on June 9, 2025, expanding derivatives trading to ~19 hours/day



6.7 Technology Modernization

BOJ rate normalization driving TONA futures growth on OSE
Euronext launched mini cash-settled government bond futures (BTP, OAT, Bund, Bono) in September 2025
Montreal Exchange CORRA futures (CRA) reached ~170K ADV in 2025 following successful BAX-to-CRA transition

1. Overview & Profile







Item
Details

Year Established
1960 (Sydney Greasy Wool Futures Exchange, predecessor); 1972 renamed Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE); 2006 merged into ASX Limited


Country / City
Australia / Sydney (Exchange Centre, 20 Bridge Street, Sydney NSW 2000)


Ownership Structure
Part of ASX Limited, which is publicly listed on its own exchange (ticker: ASX); ~50% retail investors, ~49% institutional


Parent Company / Group

Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC); Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) for clearing and settlement stability

Helen Lofthouse (appointed August 2022)

AUD 1,107.2 million (+7.0% YoY)

AUD 510.0 million (+7.5% YoY)


Derivatives Trading Platforms
ASX 24 (futures and options on interest rates, equity indices, commodities, energy, environmental products); ASX Trade (equity options — Exchange Traded Options / ETOs)


Clearing Houses
ASX Clear (equity options, equity-related derivatives); ASX Clear (Futures) (exchange-traded futures, OTC interest rate derivatives)


Listed Derivatives Instruments
Futures and options across interest rates, equity indices (SPI 200), equity options (ETOs on ~70 underlying stocks and indices), grain, energy, and environmental products


Annual Derivatives Volume (CY2025)
Interest rate futures: record Q4 2025 volumes (+23% YoY); equity derivatives: ~13.6 million futures and options/month (mid-2025); OTC Clearing: A$2.19 trillion notional in Q4 2025


OTC Interest Rate Open Interest
A$4.124 trillion notional (end December 2025)



[Source: ASX Annual Report FY2025; ASX Rates Highlights Q4 2025; ASX Equity Derivatives Statistics; ASX website, “Trade our derivatives market”]

Key Historical Milestones

1960: Sydney Greasy Wool Futures Exchange established — Australia’s first futures exchange
1972: Renamed Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE)
1979: SFE launched 90-Day Bank Accepted Bill Futures — the first financial futures contract listed outside the United States
1980: SFE introduced US dollar futures — among the first futures contracts globally to incorporate cash settlement
1983: SFE launched the All Ordinaries Share Price Index (SPI) futures contract — the first stock index futures product outside the United States
1989: SFE launched SYCOM (Sydney Computerised Overnight Market), the first after-hours electronic trading platform for an Australian exchange
1992: SFE launched 3 Year and 10 Year Commonwealth Treasury Bond Futures
1998: SFE demutualised and listed on ASX
1999: SFE transitioned to fully electronic trading, closing its floor-based open outcry trading pits
2000: SFE adopted the OM (now Nasdaq) CLICK trading platform
2005: SFE launched d-cypha Trade, its electricity and environmental derivatives trading platform
2006 (7 July): ASX merged with SFE to form ASX Limited, creating a vertically integrated multi-asset exchange group; the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) approved the merger on 24 May 2006
2010: ASX launched ASX Trade (powered by Nasdaq OMX Genium INET) for equities and equity options; latency improved from 30 milliseconds to 300 microseconds; capacity increased from 20,000 to 100,000 orders per second
2012: ASIC assumed direct market supervision of ASX and ASX 24, ending ASX’s self-regulatory role; Chi-X (now Cboe Australia) launched as a competing market
2013: ASX launched the Australian Liquidity Centre (ALC), a purpose-built data centre and co-location facility at Gore Hill, Sydney
2014: ASX established OTC clearing for interest rate derivatives via ASX Clear (Futures)
2016: ASX launched ASX 24 New Trading Platform (NTP), a technology upgrade for the derivatives trading platform
2025 (July): ASX re-established 3 Year Treasury Bond Futures tick size to 0.5 basis points (from 1 basis point); Bond-Roll De-Linking implemented to improve market microstructure
2025 (Q4): Record interest rate derivatives trading volumes — Q4 2025 up 23% vs Q4 2024
2026 (March): ASX and LSEG announced agreement to modernise and upgrade ASX 24 trading platform; target go-live first half 2028
2026 (April): CHESS Release 1 (clearing component replacement) targeted for go-live on 20 April 2026

[Source: Wikipedia, “Australian Securities Exchange”; MarketsWiki, “Australian Securities Exchange”; ASX website, “ASX Story”; ACCC media release, May 2006; ASX press releases 2025-2026; FinanceFeeds, “ASX and LSEG Agree Technology Upgrade”, March 2026; The TRADE, “ASX introduces high-speed trading platform”, 2010]

title: ASX Derivatives (Australian Securities Exchange)
text:
3. Trading Mechanism

3.1 Auction Mechanisms
Opening Auction (ASX 24): - Pre-open phase allows order entry and amendment - At session open, accumulated orders are matched at a single equilibrium price - The algorithm maximises matched volume at the equilibrium price - Separate opening auctions for day and night sessions
Opening Auction (ASX Trade — ETOs): - Pre-open from 9:50 AM to 10:00 AM AEST - Orders entered and amended but not matched - Opening price determined by equilibrium algorithm at 10:00 AM
Closing / Settlement (ASX 24): - Daily settlement prices determined based on trading activity during defined settlement windows - For bond futures: weighted average of trade prices calculated to 4 decimal places, rounded to 3 - For SPI 200: daily settlement based on fair value calculation referencing the ASX 200 closing index level


3.2 Continuous Trading

ASX 24: continuous electronic order matching during both day and night sessions
Supports outright orders and spread strategies (calendar spreads, inter-commodity spreads)
Night sessions provide near-24-hour coverage; liquidity typically thinner outside Australian business hours
ASX Trade ETOs: continuous matching from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM AEST



3.3 Price Discovery

ASX 3 Year and 10 Year Treasury Bond Futures are benchmark derivative products ranking among the most liquid and actively traded interest rate futures globally
SPI 200 futures provide overnight price discovery for the Australian equity market during the extended night session
30-Day Interbank Cash Rate Futures are the primary market instrument for pricing Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) cash rate expectations
OTC interest rate clearing enhances price transparency in AUD/NZD rates markets



3.4 Order Priority Rules / Matching Algorithms








Algorithm
Description
Application




Price-Time Priority (FIFO)
Strict price priority, then time priority at each price level
Default for all ASX 24 futures


Pro-Rata
Allocation proportional to order size at each price level
Selected options products [unverified]


Price-Time Priority
Standard FIFO matching
ASX Trade ETOs



Key Rules: - Price priority is absolute — better-priced orders always fill first - Within the same price, time priority determines allocation (FIFO) - Self-Trade Prevention (STP) functionality available - During opening routines, orders are matched at a single equilibrium price
[Source: ASX 24 Operating Rules Section 4 (February 2026); ASX 24 Trading Platform Guide v1.05 (April 2018); ASX website, “ETO crossing on ASX Trade”]

title: ASX Derivatives (Australian Securities Exchange)
text:
8. Risk Controls & Circuit Breakers

8.1 ASX Approach to Circuit Breakers
ASX does not employ market-wide circuit breakers in the style of some international exchanges (e.g., NYSE, KRX). Instead, ASX uses a combination of:

Anomalous Order Thresholds (AOTs): Reference prices updated every minute from a 2-minute VWAP; prevents aggressive orders that are more than 10% above/below the reference price
Extreme Trade Range (ETR): Unique per instrument; triggers a 2-minute trading pause if the price moves beyond the ETR threshold
These mechanisms are applied primarily on the ASX Trade (equities/ETOs) platform



8.2 Pre-Trade Risk Controls







Control
Description




Pre-Trade Risk Management (PTRM) Software
Provided as part of the ASX 24 Trading Platform; acts as a second layer of risk management


Participant Obligation
Participants are required to have their own independent risk management systems in addition to ASX PTRM


Order Size Limits
Maximum order quantity and value limits configurable per participant


Price Collars
Rejection of orders outside defined price bands from the reference price


Kill Switch
Capability for participants and clearing members to cancel all resting orders for a given account or session [unverified]





8.3 Intraday Margin Triggers

ASX Clear (Futures) triggers ad hoc intraday margin runs if:

The price change of an individual contract exceeds 100% of its margin rate, or
The ASX SPI 200 index price changes by 1% or more intraday

Intraday margin calls are issued to participants whose positions have deteriorated beyond defined thresholds



8.4 Market Volatility Measures

11.1 CHESS Replacement Project
The replacement of CHESS (Clearing House Electronic Subregister System) is ASX’s most significant technology transformation:







Milestone
Details




Original approach
DLT-based replacement using Digital Asset’s DAML platform; announced 2015


November 2022
ASX abandoned the DLT approach after cost overruns and delays; wrote off A$250 million


2023–2024
ASX began redesign using conventional technology (not DLT)


Two-phase delivery
Release 1 (clearing replacement, FIX messaging) and Release 2 (settlement and sub-register)

Replace clearing component of CHESS; introduce FIX messaging for trade registration

Published 13 March 2026

11.2 ASX 24 Platform Modernisation (LSEG Partnership)

March 2026: ASX and LSEG announced agreement to modernise and upgrade the ASX 24 derivatives trading platform
LSEG Markets Technology to provide a high-performance, low-latency platform engineered for speed, resilience, and capacity
Collaborative design and testing throughout 2026-2027
Target go-live: first half of 2028
Will replace the current ASX 24 NTP (launched 2016)



11.3 Market Microstructure Improvements (2025)

3 Year Bond Futures tick change (July 2025): Re-established minimum tick increment to 0.5 basis points (from 1 basis point), improving price granularity and tightening spreads

These changes contributed to record Q4 2025 interest rate derivatives volumes



11.4 Record Trading Volumes (2025)

Q4 2025 interest rate derivatives volumes up 14% vs Q3 2025 and up 23% vs Q4 2024

11.5 Environmental Derivatives Expansion

ASX continues to expand its environmental futures suite: ACCU Futures, NZU Futures, and LGC Futures
Physical delivery of environmental certificates through ASX Clear (Futures) accounts at relevant environmental registries
Supports Australia’s decarbonisation transition and compliance markets

D.3 Margin Framework
Clearing Houses: - ASX Clear: Clears equity options (ETOs) and equity-related derivatives - ASX Clear (Futures): Clears all ASX 24 exchange-traded futures and options, plus OTC interest rate derivatives
Initial Margin Methodology — ASX Clear (Futures): CME SPAN







Item
Details




Methodology
CME SPAN (Standard Portfolio Analysis of Risk)


Approach
Risk-based portfolio approach calculating maximum potential loss for a combined commodity (portfolio of derivatives grouped by product)


Calibration
Initial margin rates set to cover the higher of 3 standard deviations of: (a) 60-day historical distribution or (b) 252-day historical distribution of price movements; using the higher of one- or two-day movements


Components
Scanning Risk, Intracommodity Spread Charge, Intercommodity Spread Concession (credit), Short Option Minimum Charge, Delivery Risk


Margin Formula
Total Initial Margin = max(Delivery Risk + Intracommodity Spread Charge + Short Option Minimum Charge, Scanning Risk - Intercommodity Concession)


Risk Arrays
Multiple risk arrays (sets of numeric values) calculating gains and losses under different market conditions


Portfolio Recognition
Recognises intra-commodity (inter-month) and inter-commodity spread relationships


Margin Calculation Frequency
End-of-day; plus ad hoc intraday runs triggered by significant price movements



Initial Margin Methodology — ASX Clear (Equity Options): CME SPAN

ASX Clear also uses SPAN-based margining for equity options portfolios
Margin parameters calibrated to Australian equity market volatility characteristics

Variation Margin: - Marked to market daily based on settlement prices - Variation margin calls issued end-of-day; intraday calls in stressed conditions - All margin flows processed through ASX Clear (Futures) participant accounts
Intraday Margin Triggers: - Triggered if individual contract price change exceeds 100% of its margin rate - Triggered if ASX SPI 200 index changes by 1% or more intraday - ASX Clear (Futures) may issue intraday margin calls at its discretion
Acceptable Collateral: - Cash (AUD) - Commonwealth Government Securities - Bank guarantees - Other approved collateral subject to haircuts [unverified]
[Source: ASX Clear (Futures) SPAN Margining Examples; ASX website, “Margining”; RBA Assessment of ASX Clear (Futures), Standard 6: Margin (2017-2018); ASX website, “Understanding Margins — ASX Clear”; ASX Energy, “Initial Margins”]

Item
Details

The Market Operator may vary limits on an exceptional case-by-case basis; exercised infrequently

In the event of (or to prevent) an undesirable market situation, the Market Operator may instruct participants to trade in a particular manner, including holding no more than a certain number of positions


Exercise Limits
No exercise limits set under Rule 3410; exercise limits set out separately in Clearing Rules

title: China Financial Futures Exchange (CFFEX)
text:
3. Trading Mechanism

3.1 Order Matching

Matching algorithm: Price priority, time priority
All trades are conducted via CFFEX’s electronic trading system and are automatically matched
No floor trading or open outcry



3.2 Order Types







Order Type
Description




Limit Order
Specifies a maximum buy or minimum sell price


Market Order
Executes at best available price; converted to limit order if not immediately filled





3.3 Settlement

Daily mark-to-market: CFFEX performs daily settlement using the daily settlement price to clear all contracts for profits/losses, trading margin, fees, and taxes
Index Futures: Cash settled at the arithmetic average of the underlying index during the last two hours of trading on the last trading day
CGB Futures: Physical delivery of eligible government bonds



3.4 Last Trading Day

Stock Index Futures/Options: Third Friday of the expiry month (postponed to next business day if on a public holiday)
CGB Futures: Second Friday of the delivery month



3.5 Contract Months

Stock Index Futures: Current month, next month, and next two quarterly months (4 contracts listed at a time)

title: China Financial Futures Exchange (CFFEX)
text:
5. Trading System

5.1 Platform Overview
CFFEX operates a fully electronic trading platform with no floor trading. Key characteristics:

Order matching: Automatic matching based on price priority and time priority
Architecture: Centralized matching engine processing all orders sequentially
Data dissemination: Real-time market data distribution to members and authorized data vendors
System reliability: Designed for high availability with disaster recovery capabilities



5.2 Clearing & Settlement System

Central Counterparty (CCP): CFFEX itself acts as the central counterparty for all trades
Multi-tiered clearing: Risk is distributed through the tiered membership structure (trading members, trading & clearing members, general clearing members, special clearing members)
Daily settlement: Mark-to-market performed at each day’s close using the daily settlement price
Margin management: Real-time monitoring of margin levels; margin calls issued when accounts fall below maintenance levels
Settlement banks: Major Chinese commercial banks serve as designated settlement banks



5.3 PFMI Compliance
CFFEX has published its compliance with the Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (PFMI) issued by CPMI-IOSCO.
[Source: CFFEX, “Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures”, http://www.cffex.com.cn/u/cms/www/202305/311459055ti6.pdf, accessed 2026-04-07] [Source: CFFEX, “System”, http://www.cffex.com.cn/en_new/System/, accessed 2026-04-07]

title: China Financial Futures Exchange (CFFEX)
text:
Margin Framework Summary
CFFEX uses a percentage-of-contract-value margin methodology rather than a portfolio-based system like SPAN or PRISMA. Key features:

Exchange-set minimum margins serve as the floor; futures companies (brokers) typically add a buffer of 2-6 percentage points above the exchange minimum
Margin escalation: Margins are raised as contracts approach delivery/expiry
Cross-margining for CGB futures: Offsetting long/short positions in the same or different CGB products under the same client can net margins
Regulatory adjustment: CSRC and CFFEX retain the authority to adjust margin requirements in response to market conditions, as demonstrated during the 2015 crisis when margins were raised from ~10% to 40% for stock index futures
Variation margin: Collected daily through mark-to-market settlement; settlement banks facilitate transfers between members and the exchange

text:
3. Trading Mechanism

3.1 Order Matching

Matching Method: Computerized matching using price-time priority
Priority Rules: Price priority first (higher bids and lower offers matched first), then time priority (earlier orders at the same price matched first)
Opening/Closing: Opening and closing prices determined via call auction (aggregate matching); continuous trading via continuous auction during regular sessions



3.2 Order Types







Order Type
Description




Limit Order
Order to buy or sell at a specified price or better


Market Order
Order executed immediately at the best available price; any unfilled portion automatically cancelled


Market-to-Limit Order
Submitted as market order; unfilled portion converts to limit order at the last execution price [unverified]





3.3 Price Discovery

Call Auction: Used at the opening of each session; orders accumulated during pre-opening period and matched at a single price that maximizes volume
Continuous Auction: After opening, incoming orders matched against resting orders on a continuous basis
Settlement Price: The volume-weighted average price of a contract during the last hour of trading on the trading day (for iron ore and other products)



3.4 Spread Trading

DCE supports calendar spread trading (inter-month spreads) for selected products
Spread orders submitted as a single combined order

8.1 Daily Price Limits
DCE applies daily price limits to all futures contracts, calculated as a percentage of the previous trading day’s settlement price. Limits vary by product and may be adjusted during holidays or periods of high volatility.

Expansion Mechanism: - If a futures contract settles at its price limit for consecutive trading days, DCE may expand the price limit range and increase trading margin requirements - DCE can also adjust limits on an ad hoc basis before holidays or during periods of extreme market volatility (e.g., iron ore limits raised to ±10-13% with margins at 12-17% during National Day 2024 holidays)


8.2 Trading Margin Requirements
DCE requires trading margins as a percentage of contract value. Margins vary by product, contract delivery month proximity, and market conditions.

Margin Adjustment Rules: - Margins increase as a contract approaches its delivery month (stepped increases at defined intervals) - Margins increase when open interest exceeds specified thresholds - DCE raises margins before long holidays (e.g., National Day, Spring Festival, Labor Day) - The higher of the contractual margin rate or the adjusted rate applies


8.3 Position Limits

DCE imposes speculative position limits on non-hedging positions for each product
Position limits are specified as maximum number of lots per client or per non-futures-company member
Hedging positions can be approved for higher limits upon application
Large trader reporting requirements apply when positions exceed specified thresholds



8.4 Forced Liquidation

If a member’s margin falls below the required level and is not replenished by the next trading day’s opening, DCE may forcibly close positions
Positions may also be forcibly liquidated if position limits are exceeded



8.5 Risk Warning and Emergency Measures

DCE may issue risk warnings when abnormal trading activity is detected
Emergency measures include adjusting margins, price limits, position limits, or suspending trading
The exchange can invoke special measures during extreme market conditions

title: Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE)
text:
Margin Framework

Margin Methodology
DCE uses a fixed-percentage margin system (not SPAN or VaR). Trading margins are calculated as a percentage of contract value, with the percentage varying by product, delivery month proximity, position size, and market conditions.


Margin Calculation

Initial Margin = Contract Price x Contract Size x Margin Rate
Example: Iron ore at CNY 800/ton, 100 tons/lot, 10% margin = CNY 8,000 per lot



Margin Escalation Rules







Condition
Effect




Approaching Delivery Month
Margin rate increases in stepped increments (e.g., from T-3 months to delivery month)


High Open Interest
When total open interest exceeds specified thresholds, margin rate increases


Consecutive Limit Moves
If a contract settles at its price limit for consecutive days, margin increases


Holiday Periods
DCE routinely raises margins before long holidays (Spring Festival, National Day, Labor Day)


Exchange Discretion
DCE can adjust margins at any time based on market conditions





Variation Margin

Settled daily (mark-to-market) based on the daily settlement price
Settlement price is typically the volume-weighted average price of trades during the last trading hour
Gains credited and losses debited to the member’s margin account daily
If margin falls below the maintenance level, a margin call is issued; failure to replenish may result in forced liquidation



Delivery Margin

During the delivery month, margin requirements increase significantly (typically to 20-40% of contract value) [unverified — exact rates vary by product]
Both buyers and sellers must deposit delivery margins

[Source: DCE, Risk Management Measures] [Source: Shanghai Metal Market, “DCE Adjustments to Price Limit and Trading Margin Levels”, https://www.metal.com/en/newscontent/103299960] [Source: Mondovisione, “DCE Notice on Adjustments to Price Limits During 2026 New Year’s Day Holiday”, https://mondovisione.com/media-and-resources/news/dalian-commodity-exchange-notice-on-adjustments-to-price-limits-during-2026-new-20251225]

title: Eurex
text:
3. Trading Mechanism

3.1 Auction Mechanisms
Eurex employs multiple auction types within the T7 trading system:

Opening Auction: Begins the main trading phase; orders are collected in a call phase with indicative prices displayed. An uncrossing match occurs at the price that maximizes executable volume. Opening-Auction-Only orders become active and receive a new priority timestamp when the instrument enters the Opening Auction state
Closing Auction: Concentrates liquidity at the end of the main trading phase; determines the official closing price. Similar call-phase and uncrossing mechanics as the opening auction
Intraday Auction: Scheduled around midday for certain instruments; interrupts continuous trading temporarily to provide additional price discovery points
Volatility Auction: Triggered automatically when the potential trade price of an incoming order breaches configured price deviation limits (volatility interruption). The instrument moves from continuous trading into an auction call phase for orderly price discovery. The potential trade price is checked against reference prices from all executed trades within configured lookback time windows
Trade-at-Close: After the closing auction, orders can be matched continuously at the fixed closing auction price (no further price discovery)

[Source: Eurex, “Trading phases”, https://www.eurex.com/ex-en/trade/trading-hours/trading-phases]


3.2 Continuous Trading

Central limit order book (CLOB): Fully electronic order-driven market
Matching: Continuous matching of buy and sell orders throughout the trading session
Synthetic matching: Calendar spreads are matched synthetically from outright contracts; T7 Release 14.0 extended this to Butterfly and Condor strategies for STIR futures (Euribor, Euro STR)
Market makers: Supplement order book liquidity via continuous quotes; not a quote-driven market



3.3 Price Discovery

Primary price discovery occurs through the opening auction and continuous order book
Auction uncrossing algorithm: (1) Maximum executable volume, (2) Minimum surplus, (3) Reference price as tiebreaker
Closing price: Determined via closing auction; critical for derivatives settlement calculations, index calculations, and margin computation
Indicative prices: Displayed during auction call phases to guide price discovery



3.4 Order Priority Rules

Price-time priority: Standard priority rule for most Eurex products – best price first, then earliest time at the same price
Market orders have priority over limit orders
Visible over hidden: At the same price, visible order quantities have priority over hidden (iceberg reserve) quantities
Pro-rata allocation: Used for specific products (e.g., certain interest rate options and Euribor futures) where orders at the same price are filled proportionally to their size rather than by time priority [unverified – pro-rata is common on European fixed income derivatives but exact Eurex product list requires confirmation]

Note: The T7 system supports configurable matching algorithms per product, allowing the exchange to apply price-time or pro-rata matching as appropriate.

title: Eurex
text:
4. Order Types

4.1 Standard Order Types







Order Type
Description




Market Order
Executed immediately at the best available price; no price limit specified. Not supported with IOC time-in-force


Limit Order
Specifies a maximum buy price or minimum sell price; unfilled portion rests in the order book


Stop Market Order
Held at the stop server until the trigger price is reached, then released as a Market Order


Stop Limit Order
Held at the stop server until the trigger price is reached, then released as a Limit Order. Time priority counts from when the Limit order is received by Eurex after the stop is triggered





4.2 Advanced Order Types







Order Type
Description




OCO (One-Cancels-Other)
Two linked orders where execution of one automatically cancels the other


Iceberg Order
Only a portion of the total order volume is visible in the order book; a minimum of 5% of overall volume must be visible


Book or Cancel (BOC)
Order that is rejected if it would immediately match upon entry; ensures passive (maker) execution only


Opening-Auction-Only
Active only during the opening auction; automatically cancelled if not filled during the opening auction


Closing-Auction-Only
Active only during the closing auction





4.3 Time-in-Force (TIF) Options







TIF
Description




Day
Order valid for the current trading day only; cancelled at end of session


GTC (Good-Till-Cancelled)
Order remains active until explicitly cancelled or expired (maximum duration applies)


GTDate (Good-Till-Date)
Order remains active until a specified date


IOC (Immediate-Or-Cancel)
Executes immediately as much as possible; any unfilled quantity is cancelled. Not available for Market orders or Stop orders





4.4 Order Modification & Cancellation

Orders can be modified (price, quantity, TIF) or cancelled at any time during appropriate trading phases
Modifications that change the price or increase quantity result in a new time priority
Modifications that decrease quantity preserve time priority
Mass cancellation functionality available for participants to cancel all orders in a product or across all products

5. Trading System Technology – T7

5.1 Overview







Item
Details




System Name
T7 (also used for Xetra, EEX, and other Deutsche Borse Group venues)


Current Version
T7 Release 14.0 (launched November 10, 2025 for Eurex); Release 14.1 planned for May 18, 2026


Architecture
Central matching engine with distributed gateway access; partition-based architecture allowing independent scaling


Developer
Deutsche Borse AG (in-house)





5.2 Architecture

Partition-based design: Products are distributed across multiple partitions, each with its own matching engine, allowing horizontal scaling and fault isolation
Gateway types:

Partition-Specific (PS) Gateways: Route to a specific partition only; lowest latency path for order and quote management via 10 Gbit/s cross-connects
Low-Frequency (LF) Gateways: Allow access to all partitions via a single session; higher base latency (~12 microseconds additional compared to PS)

Access Layer: 10 Gbit/s switches operating in “cut-through” mode; first bytes of an ethernet frame reserve priority on the competitive network path
Matching Engine: Central deterministic matching; processes orders and quotes with sub-microsecond internal latency



5.3 Latency & Throughput







Metric
Value




Minimum infrastructure latency (market data to request)
~2,787 nanoseconds (~2.8 microseconds)


PS Gateway to Matching Engine
~1 microsecond for cross-side requests (reduced from ~45 microseconds pre-January 2025)


LF Gateway additional latency
~12 microseconds higher than PS path


Typical throughput at t_3n
~8,000 kHz


Typical throughput at t_5
~500 kHz


Typical throughput at t_7
~300 kHz



[Source: Eurex, “Insights into Trading System Dynamics”, March 2025, https://www.eurex.com/resource/blob/48918/4f724c9415d2731cfb27295db6269c9c/data/presentation_insights-into-trading-system-dynamics_en.pdf]


5.4 Technology Stack

Protocol: FIX 5.0 SP2 semantics with proprietary session layer and flat binary encoding (ETI)
Market Data: FIX/FAST encoded multicast data streams (EMDI, MDI, EOBI)
Network: 10 Gbit/s Ethernet infrastructure; mandatory TLS encryption for all interfaces (FIX LF and ETI)
GUI: New generation browser-based GUIs introduced in 2025 to replace legacy desktop applications

5.6 Disaster Recovery & Business Continuity (DR/BCP)

Primary data center: Equinix FR2, Frankfurt, Germany (houses T7 back-end and co-location facility)
DR infrastructure: T7 simulation environment serves as DR production infrastructure in the event of a disaster at the primary site
DR scenario: Renders the T7 back-end of Equinix FR2 inaccessible while co-location facility remains accessible, allowing co-location customers to still connect to DR infrastructure
Regular testing: Eurex conducts semi-annual T7 Disaster Recovery Tests (most recently October 2024, with tests in March and October each year). All Trading Participants are requested to participate

text:
8. Risk Controls & Circuit Breakers

8.1 Volatility Interruptions (Circuit Breakers)
Eurex’s primary safeguard mechanism to prevent erroneous trades and sudden price cascades:

Dynamic Volatility Interruption: The potential trade price of an incoming order is checked against all prices of previously executed trades within configured lookback time windows (reference prices)
Trigger: If the allowed price deviation is exceeded, the execution is prevented and the instrument (or all instruments in the affected product) is automatically moved from continuous trading to a volatility auction
Duration: The volatility auction runs for a defined period to allow orderly price discovery before returning to continuous trading
Price Collars: For Eurex EnLight off-book trading, price collars reject quotes or orders falling outside an entry interval defined by the Management Board. Price collars do not trigger a trading halt

[Source: Eurex, “Volatility Interruption Functionality”, https://www.eurex.com/ex-en/support/emergencies-and-safeguards/volatility-interruption-functionality]


8.2 Pre-Trade Risk Controls







Control
Description




Maximum Order Quantity / Transaction Size Limits (TSL)
Exchange-level and member-level limits on the maximum number of contracts per order/quote. The lowest limit set (by exchange, Clearing Member, or Trading Participant) applies


Maximum Order Value
Limits on the maximum notional value of a single order


Pre-Trade Risk (PTR) Limits
Clearing members can define limits for themselves and their non-clearing participants (DCMPs); monitored in real-time


Price Reasonability Checks
Orders are checked against reference prices to detect potentially erroneous prices





8.3 Post-Trade Risk Controls

Position monitoring: Real-time position monitoring by Eurex Clearing
Intraday margin calls: Eurex Clearing can directly debit Clearing Members when intraday risk thresholds are breached
Stop/Kill functionality: Emergency procedures for halting trading activity; details in the Eurex Emergency Playbook (published under Support > Emergencies and Safeguards)

[Source: Eurex, “Trading Safeguards”, October 2025, https://www.eurex.com/resource/blob/2448162/28033c3a73ea19078860573d526f8f33/data/presentation-trading-safeguards.pdf]

text:
14. Margin Framework – Eurex Clearing Prisma

14.1 Overview
Eurex Clearing Prisma is a portfolio-based risk management methodology applied to all exchange-traded derivatives (ETD) and OTC products cleared by Eurex Clearing AG. Unlike product-by-product margin calculation, Prisma determines margin requirements at the portfolio level, accounting for hedging and cross-correlation effects.


14.2 Methodology
Core Approach: - Historical Value-at-Risk (VaR): Prisma uses a filtered historical simulation approach to estimate potential portfolio losses - Liquidation Groups: Products sharing similar risk characteristics are grouped into Liquidation Groups. Portfolio margining is applied within the same Liquidation Group and with the same holding period - Example: EURO STOXX 50 Futures and DAX Futures may be in the same Liquidation Group, offering margin offsets for diversified portfolios - Cross-Product Scenarios: Enable a consistent way to account for portfolio correlation and diversification effects, resulting in more accurate risk netting - Holding Periods: Vary by product type; e.g., ETD may have a 2-day holding period while OTC IRS has a 5-day holding period


14.3 Margin Types







Margin Type
Description




Initial Margin (Additional Margin)
Covers potential liquidation risk for upcoming business days; based on Prisma historical VaR calculation at 99.x% confidence level


Premium Margin
For options: covers the cost of the option premium (traditional-style options)


Current Liquidating Margin
Reflects the immediate mark-to-market value of positions


Variation Margin
Daily settlement of profits and losses on futures positions; must be paid in cash


Margin Floors
Annual recalibration of Prisma initial margin floors (most recent recalibration effective June 16, 2025)





14.4 Cross-Margining

Cross-product margining: Offsets between products within the same Liquidation Group
Cross-market margining: Offsets between listed (ETD) and OTC positions cleared by Eurex Clearing
Cross-holding-period margining: Allows offsets between products with different holding periods (e.g., OTC IRS with 5-day holding period vs. listed fixed income with 2-day holding period)
Key benefit: More accurate risk netting leads to significantly lower initial margin requirements for diversified portfolios



14.5 Margin Call Process

Margins are calculated throughout the trading day (intraday margin recalculations)
Regular margin calls: End-of-day margin requirements communicated to Clearing Members
Intraday margin calls: Eurex Clearing can directly debit Clearing Members if intraday risk thresholds are breached
Payment: Variation margin and premiums on traditional options must be paid in cash; initial margin can be posted in cash or eligible securities (with appropriate haircuts)



14.6 Cloud Prisma Margin Estimator (cPME)

Web-based tool allowing participants to estimate margin requirements for hypothetical portfolios
Available via Deutsche Borse Risk GitHub: https://deutsche-boerse-risk.github.io/CloudPrismaMarginEstimator/

[Source: Eurex Clearing, “Eurex Clearing Prisma”, https://www.eurex.com/ec-en/services/margining/eurex-clearing-prisma] [Source: Eurex Clearing, “Margining process”, https://www.eurex.com/ec-en/services/margining/margining-process] [Source: Eurex Clearing, “Cross-margining”, https://www.eurex.com/ec-en/services/margining/cross-margining]

title: Eurex
text:
15. Position Limits

15.1 Framework

MiFID II Article 57: Establishes position limits for commodity derivatives traded on EU trading venues
BaFin is the competent authority for setting and monitoring position limits for commodity derivatives traded exclusively or predominantly on German trading venues (including Eurex)
Accountability levels: Set for financial instruments to identify large positions and ensure orderly markets



15.2 Commodity Derivatives Position Limits

Position limits set by BaFin based on deliverable supply and open interest
Apply to net positions held by any person in commodity derivatives and economically equivalent OTC contracts
Limits apply at both the spot month and the other months combined levels



15.3 Hedge Exemptions

Non-financial entities may apply for exemption from position limits under MiFID II Article 57(1) if positions are objectively measurable as reducing risks directly relating to non-financial commercial activities
Financial entities must count hedging contracts toward position limits (no hedge exemption available)
Application process: Submit to BaFin pursuant to MiFID II Article 57(1) and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/591 Article 8
Once approved, positions flagged as “hedge” fall outside the position limit regime



15.4 Non-Commodity Position Limits

For equity index and interest rate derivatives, Eurex applies position reporting requirements rather than hard position limits
Large position reporting thresholds trigger enhanced monitoring by Eurex Market Supervision
Exchange rules may impose product-specific position limits in exceptional circumstances

[Source: BaFin, “Position limits for commodity derivatives”, https://www.bafin.de/EN/Aufsicht/BoersenMaerkte/Derivate/PositionslimitsWarenderivate/positionslimits_warenderivate_node_en.html]

text:
17. Delivery & Settlement

17.1 Cash Settlement
Applies to index derivatives, volatility derivatives, dividend derivatives, money market futures:







Product Type
Final Settlement Price Determination




EURO STOXX 50 Futures/Options
Average of EURO STOXX 50 index values calculated between 11:50 and 12:00 CET on final settlement day


DAX Futures/Options
Based on intraday auction values of DAX constituent stocks on final settlement day


VSTOXX Futures
Based on VSTOXX index calculation on expiration day


Euribor / Euro STR Futures
Based on reference rate fixing on final settlement day





17.2 Physical Delivery
Applies to fixed income futures, single stock futures, equity options:
Fixed Income Futures Delivery Process: 1. Notification: Clearing members with open short positions must notify Eurex on the last trading day which specific bond (from the deliverable basket) they will deliver, by end of Post-Trading Full Period 2. Delivery day: 10th calendar day of the maturity month (or next exchange day) 3. Conversion factors: Applied to adjust for differences between the notional coupon (6%) and actual coupon of delivered bonds 4. Cheapest-to-deliver (CTD): Short position holders typically select the bond that is cheapest to deliver based on conversion factors and market conditions
Single Stock Futures/Options: - Physical delivery of underlying shares - Settlement via Eurex Clearing through the respective CSD (Clearstream or other connected settlement systems) - Delivery occurs on the standard settlement cycle (T+2 for most European markets)


17.3 Variation Margin (Daily Settlement)

Futures: Daily mark-to-market with cash variation margin payments
Daily settlement prices for current maturity months derived from volume-weighted average of trades in the minute before 17:15 CET (if >5 trades in that period)
Settlement via Eurex Clearing AG through designated payment banks

HKFE is a wholly owned subsidiary of HKEX, which is publicly traded on SEHK (stock code: 0388.HK). The Hong Kong SAR Government is the single largest shareholder with the right to appoint 6 of 13 board directors


Parent Company / Group
Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited (HKEX) – vertically integrated group comprising SEHK (cash equities), HKFE (derivatives), LME (London Metal Exchange, acquired 2012), four clearing houses (HKSCC, HKCC, SEOCH, OTC Clear), and data services

Key Historical Milestones

1976: Hong Kong Commodities Exchange established; initially traded cotton, sugar, soybean, and gold futures
1985: Renamed to Hong Kong Futures Exchange Limited (HKFE)
1986: Hang Seng Index Futures launched (became flagship product); four stock exchanges merged into Stock Exchange of Hong Kong (SEHK)
1987: October stock market crash; HKFE closed for four days; subsequent Davison Commission reforms
1989: HKFE Clearing Corporation (HKCC) assumed clearing functions, replacing the previous guarantee corporation
1993: Stock options introduced on SEHK; Hang Seng Index Options launched on HKFE
1995: HKATS (Hong Kong Futures Automatic Trading System) launched in November – electronic trading replaces open outcry
1997: H-shares Index (HSCEI) Futures launched; Asian Financial Crisis tests market resilience
1999: HKFE trading floor closed; all trading migrated to electronic HKATS platform
2000: HKFE, SEHK, and HKSCC demutualized and merged under HKEX holding company (listed June 27, 2000, stock code 0388)
2000: Mini-HSI Futures launched (October) to serve retail investors
2003: Stock Futures introduced
2008: After-Hours Futures Trading (T+1 Session) introduced
2012: HKEX acquires London Metal Exchange (LME) for GBP 1.388 billion; USD/CNH Currency Futures launched
2013: HKATS and DCASS upgraded to Nasdaq’s Genium INET platform (October), dramatically improving latency and capacity
2017: MSCI Index Futures suite launched, covering Asia and Emerging Markets
2019: HKATS upgraded to newer Genium INET version (May); LME London Metal Mini Futures introduced (August)
2020: Hang Seng TECH Index Futures and Options launched (November)
2021: MSCI China A 50 Connect Index Futures launched (October)
2023: Swap Connect (Northbound) launched (May 15) for interbank rate swaps; Weekly stock options expiries introduced (November 2024)
2024: Bonnie Chan Yiting becomes CEO (March 1); Carlson Tong Ka-shing becomes Chairman (May 3); derivatives volume sets third consecutive annual record at 334 million contracts; single-day record of 4.26 million contracts (September 27)
2025: Q1 derivatives ADV reaches quarterly record of 1,866K contracts; stock options Q1 ADV reaches record 964,803 contracts; position limit enhancements effective July 2, 2025; HKEX deploys system enhancements for increased position limits
2026 (ongoing): Continued expansion of MSCI derivatives suite; Southbound Swap Connect enhancements; RMB-denominated derivatives expansion

title: HKEX Derivatives Market
text:
3. Trading Mechanism

3.1 Pre-Market Opening Period
During the Pre-Market Opening (PMO) period (8:45–9:15 AM and 12:30–1:00 PM for index products), the system collects orders and calculates the Calculated Opening Price (COP). At the transition to continuous trading, orders are matched at the COP.

Auction Orders: Orders without a specified price, matched at COP on a time-priority basis. They have higher matching priority than limit orders during auction.
Limit Orders in PMO: Entered with a price limit and matched at the COP if the limit price is at or better than the COP.



3.2 Continuous Trading Session

Matching algorithm: Strict price/time priority – the best-priced order is matched first; among orders at the same price, earlier orders have priority.
HKATS processes orders synchronously and sequentially, one transaction at a time.
All participants receive identical execution on a centralized electronic marketplace with no time/place advantages.
Trade data is transmitted simultaneously to the relevant clearing house (HKCC or SEOCH) upon execution.



3.3 After-Hours Trading (T+1 Session)

Available for major equity index products, currency futures, and commodity futures.
Orders with the T+1 attribute remain active during the AHT session (5:15 PM – 3:00 AM HKT for index products).
Orders without the T+1 attribute are automatically inactivated during AHT and reactivated in the next regular session.
T+1 trades are cleared and settled on the next trading day.



3.4 Price Controls
Dynamic Price Banding (DPB): - Prevents erroneous orders by enforcing floating price bands around a reference price. - Reference price adjusts dynamically based on actual traded prices. - Orders outside the band are rejected.
Volatility Control Mechanism (VCM): - Applies to individual instruments (not the entire market). - Trigger level: +/- 5% from the last traded price for derivatives (compared to +/- 10% for securities). - Upon triggering, a cooling-off period is invoked during which trading continues within a price band. - The VCM applies to major products including HSI futures, HSCEI futures, HS TECH futures, and Mini variants.
Price Limit Up/Down Mechanism: - Additional price band restrictions to control extreme volatility within pre-defined ranges.


3.5 Order Priority

Price priority – Best price always executed first
Time priority – Among orders at the same price, the earliest order is executed first
Auction orders have priority over limit orders during the pre-market opening period

[Source: HKEX, “Trading Mechanism Overview”, https://www.hkex.com.hk/-/media/hkex-market/services/trading/derivatives/trading-mechanism/overview/tradingmechanismoverview_e, accessed 2026-04-06]

title: HKEX Derivatives Market
text:
4. Order Types

4.1 Standard Order Types







Order Type
Description




Limit Order (LO)
Specifies a maximum buy or minimum sell price; executes when market price reaches or improves on the limit


Auction Order (AAO)
No specified price; used exclusively during Pre-Market Opening; matched at COP with higher priority than limit orders


At-Auction Limit Order (AALO)
Limit order entered during auction periods; matched at COP if within the limit price





4.2 Advanced Order Types







Order Type
Description




Enhanced Limit Order (ELO)
Matches up to a specified number of price queues (up to 10 ticks) away from the best price; unmatched portion remains as limit order


Special Limit Order (SLO)
Similar to ELO but unmatched portion is cancelled


Stop Loss Limit Order (SLLO)
Triggered when market reaches a specified stop price; converts to a limit order


Good Till Date (GTD)
Remains active until the specified date or until executed/cancelled





4.3 Combination Orders







Order Type
Description




Standard Combination
Pre-defined strategies for roll-over activities (e.g., calendar spreads); supports Day/FAK/FOK validities


Tailor-Made Combination (TMC)
Enables creation of self-defined multi-leg futures and options strategies via a single order; matched by price/time priority like regular orders





4.4 Time-in-Force Conditions







Validity
Description




Day
Active until market close of the current trading day


FOK (Fill or Kill)
Must be fully executed immediately or entirely cancelled


FAK (Fill and Kill)
Partial execution accepted; unfilled remainder cancelled


EXP (Expiry)
Remains active until the product’s expiry date


Date (GTD)
Active until the specified trading date





4.5 Order Attributes







Attribute
Description




T+1
Order remains active through AHT (After-Hours Trading) session; without this, orders are inactivated during T+1


Give Up
Trade transferred to another specified company post-execution


Active / Inactive
Active orders sit in the Central Orderbook; Inactive orders are held locally on the participant’s system





4.6 Order Modification & Cancellation

Orders can be modified (price, quantity) or cancelled at any time during the relevant trading session.
Modifying the price of an order resets its time priority.
Quantity reduction does not affect time priority.
During the lunch break, the trading system is closed and no order entry, modification, or cancellation is permitted.

[Source: HKEX, “Trading Mechanism – Order Types”, accessed 2026-04-06]

Programmatic interface for direct system-to-system connectivity; used by algo trading and automated systems

Primary access point connecting participant systems to HKEX host servers via high-speed message bus





5.4 Network Infrastructure

Primary and Backup Central Gateways provide redundancy
Minimum hardware: one PC, two SDNet/2 lines, two routers, one switch, and application software
SDNet/2 circuits operate at 1 Gbps physical speed
Dual data center architecture (Primary + Secondary) for failover



5.5 System History



Year
Milestone




1995
HKATS launched, replacing open outcry


1999
Trading floor closed; full electronic migration


2008
After-Hours Trading (T+1) session added


2013
Migration to Nasdaq Genium INET platform (trading + clearing)


2019
Upgraded to newer Genium INET version with enhanced capacity





5.6 Disaster Recovery / Business Continuity

HKEX operates a Primary Data Center and Secondary Data Center
Failover is triggered if the Primary Data Center fails, bringing up HKATS/DCASS at the Secondary site
HKATS connectivity tests are conducted periodically to ensure failover readiness
Both OMD-D (market data) and HKATS have dual-site architecture

[Source: HKEX, “HKATS” infrastructure page, https://www.hkex.com.hk/Services/Trading/Derivatives/Infrastructure/HKATS, accessed 2026-04-06] [Source: Nasdaq, “Hong Kong Exchange Renews Contract With NASDAQ OMX and Upgrades to INET-Based Trading Platform”, 2013] [Source: Finextra, “HKEx moves derivatives clearing and trading platforms to Genium Inet”, 2013]

text:
8. Risk Controls & Circuit Breakers

8.1 Volatility Control Mechanism (VCM)







Parameter
Details




Scope
Applies to individual instruments (not market-wide)


Trigger Level
+/- 5% from the last traded price (dynamic, not static)


Cooling-Off Period
Trading continues within a restricted price band during cool-off


Applicable Products
HSI Futures/Options, Mini-HSI, HSCEI Futures/Options, Mini-HSCEI, HS TECH Futures/Options


Design Philosophy
Triggered infrequently; intended only for extreme moves





8.2 Dynamic Price Banding (DPB)

Floating bands around a reference price (adjusted after each trade)
Orders outside the band are automatically rejected
Prevents erroneous “fat finger” orders from distorting the market
Reference price resets with actual trade executions



8.3 Price Limit Up/Down Mechanism

Pre-defined price ranges restrict trading within allowable bounds
Applied to specific products to control extreme volatility
Works in conjunction with VCM and DPB



8.4 Pre-Trade Risk Management (PTRM)

PTRM System is integrated into HKATS
Manages trading risk at the participant level before orders enter the central order book
Features include order size limits, position limits, and margin-based controls
Clearing Participants can set risk parameters for their Non-Clearing Participants



8.5 Self-Match Prevention (SMP)

Prevents a participant’s buy and sell orders from matching against each other
Helps compliance with wash-trade regulations



8.6 Error Trade Handling

Error Trade Handling Procedures for handling trades executed at erroneous prices
Large-Scale Error Trade Handling Procedures for systemic issues affecting multiple trades
Exchange may cancel or adjust trades under prescribed rules



8.7 Kill Switch

Exchange and Clearing Participants have the ability to cancel all orders for a participant in emergency situations
HKEX can suspend trading in individual products or market-wide if necessary

[Source: HKEX, “Trading Mechanism – Volatility Control Mechanism”, accessed 2026-04-06] [Source: HKEX/SFC, “Volatility Control Mechanism and Closing Auction Session Consultation”, 2015]

9. Regulatory Framework

9.1 Supervising Authorities







Authority
Role




Securities and Futures Commission (SFC)
Primary regulator for Hong Kong securities and futures markets under the Securities and Futures Ordinance (SFO, Cap. 571)


Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA)
Regulates banks’ derivatives activities; co-supervises OTC derivatives reporting


Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB)
Government policy authority for financial markets


HKEX (as SRO)
Self-regulatory organization functions including exchange rule enforcement, market surveillance, and disciplinary actions





9.2 Key Regulations







Regulation
Scope




Securities and Futures Ordinance (SFO, Cap. 571)
Primary legislation governing securities and futures markets, licensing, market conduct, and enforcement


Securities and Futures (Contracts Limits and Reportable Positions) Rules (Cap. 571Y)
Statutory position limits and large open position reporting


HKFE Rules
Exchange rules governing trading conduct, position limits (Rules 628, 633), block trades, and market integrity


Options Trading Rules
Exchange rules governing stock options trading and market making


Securities and Futures (OTC Derivatives – Reporting and Record Keeping) Rules
OTC derivatives reporting regime (enhanced regime effective September 29, 2025)





9.3 Market Surveillance

HKEX operates dedicated market surveillance systems monitoring real-time trading activity
Surveillance covers abnormal price movements, unusual volume, potential market manipulation, and insider trading
Automated alerts trigger investigation by compliance teams
HKEX Rule Enforcement conducts disciplinary proceedings for rule breaches



9.4 Reporting Requirements

Large Open Position (LOP) Reporting: Required when positions exceed specified thresholds (see Section on Position Limits below)
Transaction Reporting: All derivatives trades automatically reported to the clearing house
OTC Derivatives Reporting: Enhanced regime from September 2025 requires Unique Transaction Identifier (UTI), Unique Product Identifier (UPI), Critical Data Elements (CDE), and ISO 20022 format
Short Position Reporting: Applicable to stock-related positions



9.5 Cross-Border Arrangements







Initiative
Description




Stock Connect (Northbound/Southbound)
Mutual market access for equities with Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges (launched 2014/2016)


Swap Connect (Northbound)
Access to mainland China’s interbank rate swap market via OTC Clear, CFETS, and SHCH (launched May 2023)


Bond Connect
Access to China’s interbank bond market (launched 2017)


Mutual Recognition of Funds
Cross-border fund distribution with mainland China


MSCI Derivatives
Licensed MSCI index derivatives providing offshore hedging for China and Asia exposure



Stock Connect volumes reached record half-yearly highs in 1H 2025, driven by increased participation by international and mainland China investors.

11. Recent Developments

11.1 Record Trading Volumes (2024–2025)

2024 Full Year: 334 million derivatives contracts traded – third consecutive record year. Stock options ADV reached record 720,297 contracts. Single-day volume record of 4.26 million contracts (September 27, 2024).
Q1 2025: Quarterly record ADV of 1,866K contracts (+24% YoY). Stock options ADV reached record 964,803 contracts (+50% YoY). Stock options open interest reached daily record of 19,697,919 contracts (March 27, 2025).
Q3 2025 YTD: Stock options nine-month ADV record of 886,323 contracts (+27% YoY). HS TECH Index Futures Options OI reached daily record of 172,961 contracts (September 18, 2025). HS TECH Index Options OI reached record 132,130 contracts (September 26, 2025).



11.2 Product Launches & Enhancements

Weekly Stock Options Expiries introduced November 2024 for selected contracts, increasing flexibility for short-term hedging
New Stock Option Classes announced February 2025 for March listing
MSCI Index Derivatives Suite continues expansion with new single-country and regional contracts
MSCI China A 50 Connect Index Futures (launched October 2021) – key product for offshore A-share hedging
Hang Seng TECH Index Derivatives (launched November 2020) – growing rapidly with record OI levels in 2025



11.3 Regulatory Changes

Enhanced Position Limits for three Hang Seng Index derivative product suites effective July 2, 2025 (following December 2023 initial changes and SFC adjustments)
OTC Derivatives Reporting Enhancement effective September 29, 2025: mandatory UTI, UPI, CDE, and ISO 20022 adoption
Swap Connect Enhancements in 2024 increased participation; Southbound functionality targeting future rollout



11.4 Strategic Initiatives

Mainland China Connectivity: Continued deepening of Stock Connect, Bond Connect, and Swap Connect; expansion of RMB-denominated product offerings
RMB Dual-Counter Listings expanded post-June 2023; target rollout of additional RMB counters and derivatives across 2024–2026
LME Integration: London Metal Mini Futures on HKEX providing Asian-hours access to base metals; battery-materials contracts in development
Technology Roadmap: Automation across Connect mechanisms, settlement efficiency improvements, and API-first services for brokers and fintechs
ESG/Sustainability: Development of carbon and green finance-related products aligned with regional decarbonization mandates [unverified]

CEO: Bonnie Chan Yiting (since March 1, 2024)
Chairman: Carlson Tong Ka-shing (since May 3, 2024)

July 2, 2025: Further increases to position limits for three Hang Seng Index derivative product suites, with HKEX system enhancements deployed to support the changes

[Source: HKEX, “Large Open Positions and Position Limits”, https://www.hkex.com.hk/Services/Trading/Derivatives/Overview/Trading-Mechanism/Large-Open-Positions-and-Position-Limits, accessed 2026-04-06] [Source: HKEX FAQ, “Position Limits and Large Open Position Reporting”, accessed 2026-04-06] [Source: SFC, “Guidance Note on Position Limits and Large Open Position Reporting Requirements”, accessed 2026-04-06]



D5. Block Trading Rules

Overview
The Block Trade Facility enables large privately negotiated transactions executed outside the central order book but cleared through the clearing house, providing price certainty, execution certainty, and CCP guarantee.


Eligible Products
All HKFE and SEHK derivatives products except: - Listed combination orders - Mini-HSI futures and options - Mini-HSCEI futures and options


Minimum Volume Thresholds (MVT)



Product
MVT (contracts)




HSI/HSCEI Futures (front 4 months)
100


HSI/HSCEI Futures (back months)
50


Stock Index Futures (other)
100


Stock Futures
100


Stock Options
500


MSCI Index Futures
25 – 50 (varies by product)


Currency Futures
50


Gold/Silver Futures
30


HSI Volatility Index Futures
[unverified]





Pricing Rules

Execution prices must be “fair and reasonable”
Must fall within specified permissible price ranges:

Stock Index Futures: 1–3% (depending on contract maturity)
Stock Futures/Options: 3% or maximum market maker spread (whichever narrower)
MSCI Futures: 3%
Currency Futures: 3%
HSI Volatility Index Futures: 1%




Order Entry Windows

Stock Index Futures/Options: 4:30 PM – 4:45 PM on regular trading days
Stock Futures/Options: 4:00 PM – 4:25 PM on regular trading days
MSCI Futures referencing official closing values: within 30 minutes of next session opening



Clearing & Registration

Registration occurs only after clearing house validation
If no rejection notice within 30 minutes: block trade deemed registered
Clearing house may call additional margin if price appears unreasonable or triggers 25% margin erosion (HKCC) or 50% (SEOCH)



Information Dissemination

Block trade prices are excluded from: day-high, day-low, last traded price, and settlement price calculations
Trades marked “EMP 1 BR” or “EMP D BR” in HKATS
Volume included in overall daily statistics



Record Keeping

Participants must retain telephone recordings of all block trade orders and confirmations for at least 3 months
Evidence must be provided to the Exchange upon request

Note: HKEX does not currently operate a formal EFP (Exchange for Physical) or EFS (Exchange for Swap) facility comparable to CME Group. Off-exchange transactions are primarily handled through the Block Trade Facility. [unverified – participants should consult current HKFE Rules for latest provisions]
[Source: HKEX, “Block Trade Facility”, https://www.hkex.com.hk/Services/Trading/Derivatives/Overview/Trading-Mechanism/Block-Trade-Facility, accessed 2026-04-06]



D6. Delivery & Settlement Process

Cash-Settled Products (Index Futures/Options, HIBOR, Iron Ore)







Step
Details




Daily Settlement Price
Published by HKEX at end of each trading day


Variation Margin
Calculated daily; settled via HKCC/SEOCH bank account transfers


Final Settlement Price (HSI/HSCEI/HSTECH)
Average of index quotations at 5-minute intervals during SEHK continuous trading session + the close on the last trading day


Final Settlement Day
Business day following the last trading day


Money Settlement
Direct Debit/Credit instructions issued by HKCC to Settlement/Designated Banks





Physically Delivered Products (Stock Futures/Options, Currency Futures, Gold Futures)







Step
Details




Stock Options Exercise
By 6:30 PM on any business day (American-style); auto-exercise for ITM at expiry


Stock Delivery
Physical delivery of underlying shares via CCASS (Central Clearing and Settlement System); settlement T+2


Currency Futures
Physical delivery of CNH (for USD/CNH, EUR/CNH, etc.) on the third business day after the last trading day


Gold Futures
Physical delivery of gold at designated vault; loco Hong Kong delivery


Silver Futures
Physical delivery of silver at designated vault





Settlement Cycle

Derivatives margin/variation: T+0 (same day) for regular margin calls; intra-day calls possible
Cash settlement: T+1 (next business day after last trading day) for final settlement of index futures
Physical delivery: T+2 for stock options; T+3 for currency futures
Gold delivery: As specified in contract rules



Default Management

HKCC and SEOCH act as CCP – guarantee settlement of all transactions
Reserve Fund contributions from Clearing Participants provide first-loss absorption
Waterfall: Defaulting participant’s margin and collateral -> Reserve Fund contribution -> HKCC/SEOCH own resources -> Non-defaulting participants’ Reserve Fund contributions
HKEX has the power to suspend trading and impose emergency measures

[Source: HKEX, “Clearing Services – Listed Derivatives Overview”, accessed 2026-04-06] [Source: HKEX, “Clearing, Settlement and Collateral Management FAQ”, accessed 2026-04-06]

3. Trading Mechanism

3.1 Auction Types
Opening Single-Price Auction (개시단일가): - First portion of regular and night sessions - Accumulated orders are matched at a single price that maximizes matched volume - Random end period applied to prevent manipulation
Closing Single-Price Auction (종가단일가): - Last 10 minutes of regular and night sessions (15:35–15:45 KST for regular session) - Settlement price determined through single-price auction algorithm - Random end period applied
Intraday Volatility Interruption: - Triggers a temporary single-price auction when dynamic or static VI thresholds are breached - 2-minute cooling-off period followed by single-price auction


3.2 Continuous Trading

Price-Time Priority (가격우선·시간우선): Standard FIFO matching — best-priced orders fill first; among orders at the same price, earliest order fills first
Order-driven market: No specialist or dealer system; all liquidity comes from public and market maker orders
Pure electronic matching via EXTURE+ platform



3.3 Price Discovery

Opening price: Determined by single-price auction algorithm at session open
Settlement price: Last traded price during the settlement window (or VWAP method for final settlement in some products)
Final settlement price for KOSPI 200: Weighted average of component stock opening prices during the last 30 minutes of trading on the last trading day, calculated to prevent manipulation
Implied pricing: Not supported — KRX uses direct order book matching only (unlike CME Globex’s implied spread functionality)

[Source: KRX, “파생상품시장 업무규정_전문_20250609”]

8. Risk Controls & Circuit Breakers
From 업무규정 and 시행세칙:

8.1 Static Price Limits (Daily)







Product
Price Limit

8.2 Dynamic VI (Volatility Interruption, 동적VI)

Triggered when execution price deviates +/-3% or more from the reference price (for KOSPI 200 futures)
Results in a 2-minute cooling-off period followed by a single-price auction
Applies to both futures and options contracts
Reference price updated after each VI event



8.3 Static VI (정적VI)

Triggered when price deviates beyond the previous day’s settlement price by a specified percentage
Results in a trading halt followed by a single-price auction
Thresholds vary by product



8.4 Market-wide Circuit Breaker (Sidecar)

KOSPI 200 Futures Sidecar: When lead-month futures price reaches +/-5% of previous settlement AND remains for 1 minute with theoretical price variance +/-3% or more
Results in a 5-minute halt of ALL derivatives contracts
Three levels: 5% -> 10% -> 20%
Each level can only be triggered once per day



8.5 Pre-trade Risk Controls

Maximum order size limits per member
Intraday margin monitoring with real-time position tracking
Real-time position limit checks
Kill switch capabilities for member firms
Automated risk parameter checks before order acceptance

Key Historical Milestones

1992: NSE incorporated as a tax-paying company; India’s first electronic exchange
1994 (November): NSE commences equity cash market trading
2000 (12 June): F&O segment launched — index futures on Nifty 50 begin trading, making NSE one of India’s first derivatives exchanges
2001 (4 June): Index options on Nifty 50 introduced
2001 (2 July): Options on individual securities launched
2001 (9 November): Futures on individual securities launched — completing the four basic F&O product types
2008 (August): Currency derivatives segment launched (USD/INR futures)
2010: Interest rate futures on government securities introduced
2018 (October): Commodity derivatives segment launched (gold, silver futures)
2018 (February): Cross-currency futures and options (EUR-USD, GBP-USD, USD-JPY) introduced; options on EUR/INR, GBP/INR, JPY/INR launched
2019: NSE becomes the world’s largest derivatives exchange by contract volume (FIA), a title it held for five consecutive years (2019–2024)
2021 (phased, March–September): SEBI peak margin rules fully implemented — 100% upfront margin required for all intraday F&O positions
2023 (3 July): NSE International Exchange (NSE IX) at GIFT City goes operational; GIFT Nifty replaces SGX Nifty
2023: NSE trades ~85 billion derivatives contracts — more than 10x the second-largest exchange (B3, at 8.3 billion)
2024 (September): SEBI publishes updated study: 93% of individual F&O traders incurred losses between FY22–FY24, with aggregate losses exceeding Rs 1.8 lakh crore
2024 (October–November): SEBI announces six major measures to curb F&O speculation (effective November 2024–February 2025)
2024 (November 20): Weekly expiry restrictions and increased lot sizes take effect
2025 (H1): NSE loses #1 global derivatives exchange ranking to Brazil’s B3, attributed to SEBI-mandated volume curbs and B3’s smaller contract sizes
2026 (April, planned): Launch of Platts oil price benchmark derivatives (Dated Brent Crude Oil futures)

[Source: NSE — History & Milestones; StockEdge — NSE’s 30-Year Evolution; SEBI Press Release, September 2024; Business Standard — NSE Loses Top Spot to B3; Zerodha — SEBI’s New Rules]

8. Risk Controls & Circuit Breakers

8.1 Market-Wide Circuit Breakers (Index-Based)
Market-wide circuit breakers are triggered by movement of either the BSE Sensex or the Nifty 50, whichever is breached first. When triggered, trading halts across all equity and equity derivative markets nationwide (NSE, BSE, and other exchanges).










Level
Trigger
Halt if Before 1:00 PM
Halt if 1:00–2:30 PM
Halt if After 2:30 PM




Level 1
10% index movement
45-minute halt
15-minute halt
No halt


Level 2
15% index movement
1 hour 45 minutes
45-minute halt
Remainder of day


Level 3
20% index movement
Remainder of day
Remainder of day
Remainder of day



Circuit breaker limits are recalculated daily based on the previous day’s closing level of the index, rounded to the nearest tick size.
[Source: NSE — Circuit Breakers; Business Standard — Circuit Filters Explained]


8.2 Price Bands for Derivatives Underlyings

Price bands are not applicable to securities on which derivative products are available
Instead, the exchange applies a dynamic price band of 10% of the previous day’s closing price, which is flexed based on pre-defined criteria as the underlying moves

[Source: NSE — Circuit Breakers]


8.3 Pre-trade Risk Controls

Quantity freeze: Orders exceeding a predefined quantity threshold require manual confirmation by the exchange
Order value limits: Maximum order value checks
Position limits: Market-wide position limits (MWPL) and trading member-level limits
Real-time margin monitoring: Intraday position monitoring and margining on a real-time basis



8.4 Expiry Day Extreme Loss Margin (from November 2024)
An additional Extreme Loss Margin (ELM) of 2% is applied to short options positions on the expiry day, to cover heightened volatility risk.
[Source: Zerodha — SEBI’s New Rules; Outlook Business — SEBI’s New F&O Rules]

Details

Individual stock futures and options permitted

Phased implementation requiring 100% upfront margin for all intraday F&O positions; random snapshots taken 4–5 times daily; penalty for shortfall


2024 (Sep)
SEBI Study on Retail F&O Losses
Updated study revealed 93% of individual traders incurred losses in equity F&O between FY22–FY24; aggregate losses exceeded Rs 1.8 lakh crore over three years


2024 (Oct)
SEBI Six-Point F&O Reform Package
Comprehensive measures to curb retail speculation

Upfront premium collection

[Source: SEBI — Press Release, September 2024; Business Standard — SEBI Announces Six Key Changes; Zerodha — SEBI’s New Rules; Bajaj Broking — SEBI Peak Margin Rules]


9.3 Impact of SEBI Curbs

Volume decline: Derivatives trading volumes fell ~30–38% from their peak following the November 2024 curbs
Retail participation decline: Smaller investor participation in derivatives dropped ~49% (Icra estimate)
Global ranking lost: NSE ceded #1 derivatives exchange title to Brazil’s B3 in H1 2025
Policy rationale: Protection of retail investors, given that 93% incurred losses and aggregate losses exceeded Rs 1.8 lakh crore in FY22–FY24

[Source: Business Standard — Derivatives Trading Drops 38%; Business Standard — Small Investors Decline 49%; Angel One — NSE Loses Top Title]


9.4 Market Surveillance

NSE operates a dedicated surveillance department monitoring trading patterns, price movements, and position concentrations
Automated alerts for unusual trading activity, insider trading patterns, and market manipulation
SEBI mandates large trader reporting for positions exceeding specified thresholds

text:
Margin Framework

Margin Methodology
NSE Clearing uses the SPAN (Standard Portfolio Analysis of Risk) system — a portfolio-based margining system originally developed by CME Group. SPAN estimates risk across combined futures and options portfolios and revalues positions under various scenarios of changing market conditions.


Margin Components







Component
Description




SPAN Margin (Initial Margin)
Based on 99% VaR over a one-day time horizon; calculated using worst-case portfolio loss across 16 risk scenarios


Exposure Margin
Additional margin for potential exposure; typically 3% for index F&O, 5–10% for stock F&O


Extreme Loss Margin (ELM)
Covers losses beyond normal VaR scenarios


Expiry Day ELM
Additional 2% on short options positions on expiry day (from November 2024)


Mark-to-Market (MTM)
Daily settlement of profit/loss; collected on T+1 basis


Delivery Margin
Applied to physically settling stock options contracts nearing expiry





SEBI Peak Margin Rules (September 2021 — Full Implementation)







Aspect
Requirement




Minimum margin
100% of SPAN + Exposure margin required at all times (including intraday)


Monitoring
Random snapshots of positions at 4–5 intervals during the trading day


Penalty
Shortfall penalty charged if margin is insufficient at any snapshot


Impact
Eliminated excessive intraday leverage previously offered by brokers; brokers can no longer provide additional leverage beyond SPAN margins





Upfront Premium Collection (February 2025)
Option buyers must pay the entire option premium upfront. Previously, some brokers allowed intraday leverage on option purchases. This rule eliminated that practice.


Interest Rate Futures Margins







Product
Initial Margin




GOI Security Futures (NBF II)
1.5% of contract value (subject to max 2.8% on first day)


91-Day T-Bill Futures
0.10% of notional value on first trading day



[Source: NSE Clearing — SPAN; NSE Clearing — Margins; NSE — SPAN Risk Parameters; Bajaj Broking — SEBI Peak Margin Rules; NSE — Interest Rate Futures Margins]
